articles.title: Will Najib Razak be transferred to house arrest?
articles.summary: Malaysia’s king and government in a standoff after attorney general disputed order allowing former PM to leave jail.
articles.body:
A royal order, a jailed former prime minister, and a dispute over who has the final say.

Malaysia’s king has warned the government not to challenge his authority in Najib Razak’s transfer to house arrest.

Razak was due to leave prison after his party paid a $12m fine as part of the conditions of his royal pardon.

But the transfer was suspended after the attorney general sought clarification on the court order.

Najib is appealing a separate 15-year sentence for abuse of power and money laundering.

So, what is behind the standoff between Malaysia’s monarchy and government?

articles.title: Cyprus rivals agree new crossings across island’s dividing line
articles.summary: The island has been split since 1974, when Turkiye invaded and seized the northern part after a coup by the Greeks.
articles.body:
Greek Cypriot and Turkish Cypriot leaders have agreed ⁠to open two ⁠new border crossings, coordinate emergency responses, and share archival materials as part of a United Nations-backed effort to resume ⁠peace talks on the divided island.

Greek Cypriot leader Nikos Christodoulides and Turkish Cypriot leader Tufan Erhurman jointly met with United Nations special envoy Maria Angela Holguin on Monday in the UN-controlled buffer zone that splits the island. The agreement is the first concrete sign of detente between the rivals after nearly a decade of deadlock.

The UN said in a statement that Monday’s meeting was “positive” and that the two leaders would talk again in the coming weeks in the presence of outgoing UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres.

“We are continuing this effort with absolute seriousness and one single goal: resuming the talks before the ‌end ‌of the secretary-general’s term,” at the end of the year, Christodoulides told reporters after the meeting.

Guterres began a new drive to try to resolve the more than five-decade-old conflict in the summer, suggesting new crossings could build trust and confidence. However, the two sides have since been disagreeing ‌over the ground rules for talks.

The move would bring the number of open crossings on the divided Mediterranean island to 11, according ⁠to media in Cyprus.

Cyprus was split in 1974 when Turkiye invaded and seized the northern part in response to a coup instigated by the then-military government in Greece.

A previous power-sharing administration of Greek and Turkish Cypriots had fallen apart in 1963, and a UN Peacekeeping Force has monitored a 180km (112-mile) ceasefire line which splits the two sides since.

Only Turkiye recognises the northern part of the island as an independent republic. Ankara maintains more than 35,000 troops on Cyprus.

Decades of talks have repeatedly failed to reunify Cyprus , with the last official round collapsing in 2017. Greek Cypriots are against Ankara having any hands-on involvement; Turkish Cypriots say it is essential.

Last year, the north elected its first pro-unification leader since 2020, generating renewed hope.

articles.title: Glycerin vs. hyaluronic acid: Which ingredient should we be using this winter?
articles.summary: Glycerin and hyaluronic acid are both common ingredients in your favorite hydrating skin care — I asked a dermatologist to find out which works better for dry skin.
articles.body: When it comes to dry skin, hyaluronic acid and glycerin are two ingredients you’ve probably come across in your favorite moisturizers, serums, cleansers and more. But what does each ingredient really do, and more importantly — which is best for dry skin? I spoke to Dr. Michele Green, a board-certified cosmetic dermatologist in New York City, to find out the differences, along with which of the two you should be reaching for during the winter season. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. What is glycerin? Glycerin (also known as glycerol) is a naturally-occuring humectant, meaning it pulls water from the deeper layers of the skin and binds it to the skin’s outer layers, says Green. “It occurs naturally in the skin as part of the moisturizing system that keeps the outer layer, called the stratum corneum, soft and flexible,” she says. It’s a clear, odorless, liquid that supports a healthy skin barrier and improves texture, which is why it’s such a popular skin care ingredient. When used cosmetically, it’s usually derived from plant oils like coconut, soy or palm, and can be found in cleansers, serums, moisturizers and more, says Green. What is hyaluronic acid? Hyaluronic acid is a sugar molecule that the body naturally produces and stores in the skin, eyes, joint and connective tissue, says Green. It’s often listed on labels as sodium hyaluronate, and like glycerin, is a humectant that’s great for helping drier skin stay dewy. It can hold up to 1,000 times its weight in moisture, and when applied to damp skin, it locks in all that water to keep your skin hydrated. What’s the difference between glycerin and hyaluronic acid? Glycerin and hyaluronic acid differ in their molecular size, texture and cost. Glycerin is a small molecule that penetrates the skin’s layers, whereas hyaluronic acid is usually much larger and sits closer to the skin’s surface, says Green. Despite that, hyaluronic acid still tends to have a more lightweight texture than glycerin, which is usually stickier or heavier (which is part of why hyaluronic acid is used in so many serums, says Green). Glycerin is also usually derived from plant oils or made synthetically, making it more affordable, whereas hyaluronic acid is usually made via bacterial fermentation and is more expensive, says Green. Is glycerin or hyaluronic acid better for dry skin? Glycerin is considered the better choice for dry skin, since it reaches into the deeper layers of the skin, whereas hyaluronic acid mainly hydrates the surface. Dry skin is usually caused by a weaker moisture barrier and lack of natural oils, so it benefits most from an ingredient like glycerin that helps to repair it, says Green. Hyaluronic acid, on the other hand, is better for dehydrated skin that lacks water rather than oil, since it helps draw water to the surface, she says. The best hyaluronic acid and glycerin products These products have glycerin, hyaluronic acid or both, and come recommended by Green and NBC Selected editors. Best overall Green recommends this moisturizer from Cerave, which made our best 100 moisturizers list, for its hydrating formula that combines hyaluronic acid, glycerin and three essential ceramides for top-tier barrier support. It can be used on the face and body, plus it’s been approved by the National Eczema Association, according to the brand. “It’s an excellent choice for dry, sensitive, and eczema-prone skin that needs both hydration and barrier repair,” says Green. Best essence When it comes to hydration, this lightweight essence has held me down since college, and if I was limited to using one Cosrx product for the rest of my life, it would be this one. It has a high concentration of hyaluronic acid and sea buckthorn oil to strengthen the skin barrier, and acts as a toner, essence and serum all in one. I also love that it keeps my oily skin hydrated without any extra greasiness — perfect for getting the dewy look without having to worry about oiliness or buildup that may cause acne. Best moisturizer for dry skin NBC Selected reporter Zoe Malin uses this La Roche-Posay moisturizer on her dry, acne-prone skin daily, and loves how well-balanced the formula is. “It has a medium thickness, so it’s moisturizing enough to prevent dry, flaky skin, yet thin enough that it absorbs quickly,” she says. “It never makes me look oily or shiny, and it never exacerbates irritation when I’m experiencing it.” It’s formulated with three ceramides, and includes niacinamide and glycerin for barrier-strength support. Best cleanser Farmacy’s cleansing balm is an NBC Selected staff favorite — I love using it to help remove makeup, or for double-cleansing when my skin feels especially congested. Along with compounded glycerin, the formula includes an antioxidant blend and papaya extract to help target bumps and blemishes, along with sunflower oil to help melt down makeup and grease, according to the brand. Plus, this fragrance-free version is great for sensitive skin. Best moisturizer for oily skin The gel texture of this moisturizer is great for oily skin, since it has a lightweight finish that won’t feel heavy or greasy on the skin. The hyaluronic acid in the formula helps water to bind to your skin’s surface, and it’s noncomedogenic, so it also won’t clog your pores, according to the brand. Although the formula is safe for sensitive skin, it does have added fragrance. Best splurge This cream from Tatcha combines antioxidants and hyaluronic acid for deep moisture, along with squalane to keep the hydration sealed in longer, according to the brand. Dr. Annie Chiu, a board-certified cosmetic dermatologist whorecommends this moisturizer in our guide to moisturizers for dry skin, and says it has an “elegant, non-greasy formula” that’s also noncomedogenic. Best serum Not only does this concentrated serum include 30% glycerin, it also has polyglutamic acid, which is a powerful humectant for holding water in the skin. It also includes niacinamide to help repair the moisture barrier, and soothing allantoin to calm irritated, sensitive skin, according to the brand. It has a lightweight, slightly sticky texture, and reviewers especially love how quickly it absorbs into the skin and how well it layers with makeup and other skin care products. How to shop for hydrating skin care Who is glycerin best for? Dry skin: Glycerin is great for dry, flaky skin that may have a weaker moisture barrier, since it permeates the skin to repair the barrier, says Green. “It is also an excellent choice for eczema-prone skin and skin irritated by harsh weather, over-cleansing, or active treatments such as retinoids,” she says. She also says it’s great for the wintertime when skin tends to get chronically dry.Sensitive skin: “Glycerin is often the preferred option for sensitive skin,” says Green. “It is one of the most gentle and well-tolerated skin care ingredients,” she says. Its barrier-strengthening properties can also help to reduce irritation and redness that sensitive skin is usually more prone to. Who is hyaluronic acid best for? Dehydrated skin: If your skin is dull, or feeling tight or stiff, hyaluronic acid may be just what you need. Green suggests it for dehydrated skin that needs smoothing and hydrating, since it reduces the look of fine lines and texture caused by a lack of moisture. The thin texture also makes it great for layering underneath makeup in serum or moisturizer form, she says.Oily skin: The lightweight texture of hyaluronic acid makes it ideal for oily skin, which tends to produce more oil to compensate for the lack of hydration, says Green. “Hyaluronic acid provides lightweight, water-based hydration that absorbs quickly without leaving a greasy or heavy residue,” she says. It’s also noncomedogenic, so it won’t clog the pores of those with acne-prone skin (glycerin is also noncomedogenic, however it can have a tacky texture that oily skin may not work as well with, says Green).Mature skin: Hyaluronic acid is especially useful for mature skin, since the body naturally produces less of it with age, says Green. This directly affects dryness, loss of firmness, fine lines and more, and hyaluronic acid can act as a solution in helping to topically replace the moisture in your skin. However, for best results Green recommends combining glycerin and hyaluronic acid to get both the surface-level and deeper hydrating effects of each. articles.title: Virginia community farm installs 42 solar panels above crops and wins North American Solar Farm of the Year, generating 130% of its electricity needs without giving up farmland
articles.summary: Virginia agrivoltaics project, the Community Farm at Roundabout Meadows installed 42 solar panels above working crop rows, and the pilot has since been
articles.body: Virginia agrivoltaics project, the Community Farm at Roundabout Meadows installed 42 solar panels above working crop rows, and the pilot has since been named a co-recipient of the Solar Farm of the Year award. Run by a land conservation organisation in the Virginia Piedmont, the farm shows that food production and clean electricity can share the same ground. The project launched in October 2025, and its solar garden occupies only a quarter-acre corner of the eight-acre site. That small footprint produces more electricity than the farm uses, with panels high enough for crops to grow beneath them in raised planter boxes.Why the Community Farm at Roundabout Meadows won North American Solar Farm of the YearAccording to The Piedmont Environmental Council, the farm shares the award with Sandbox Solar’s vitivoltaics project in Colorado, which places a solar canopy over grapevines. The award is one of the annual North American Agrivoltaics Awards, presented by Solar Farm Summit. It described the Virginia pilot as the state’s first crop-farming agrivoltaics project and an outstanding example of a community-oriented solar farm.Chris Miller, the council’s president, said in the announcement that the farm team had shown how Virginia’s farmers could achieve energy independence and help the state meet its clean energy goals while continuing to farm their land. The award was due to be presented to Ashish Kapoor, the council’s senior energy and climate advisor, and Teddy Pitsiokos, the farm manager, at a ceremony at Solar Farm House in Chicago on 27 October.How panels mounted 6 to 8 feet high generate about 130 per cent of the farm’s electricity needsThe panels hover 6 to 8 feet above crops planted in rows and in raised planter boxes. Together they generate roughly 130 per cent of what the farm uses. A backup battery system gives the farm full energy independence, so it can run on solar power and batteries alone for extended periods.The council also pointed to a wider benefit. When several farms, businesses and homes use battery backup, the energy they produce and store together can function as a virtual power plant. That supports decentralised power generation, reduces the impact of new transmission and generation, and can compensate owners for what they contribute to the grid.Tours and workshops have drawn farmers, installers, developers and policymakers to the farmPitsiokos said in the announcement that solar energy and agriculture do not have to be at odds. In his words, the panels do not displace food production, and their shade helps the farm grow kale, lettuce, beets, broccoli, garlic and more. He added that cutting the farm’s electricity bill to zero was a welcome bonus.The farm has hosted numerous tours and workshops for visitors keen to learn how distributed generation can work on farms, wineries, chicken houses and grazing operations across Virginia.The project has also fed into law-making. In June, Virginia’s governor and lawmakers marked a ceremonial bill signing at the farm, recognising a detailed definition of agrivoltaics developed by the council and the Virginia Farm Bureau. Kapoor said in the announcement that the project was informing the growing policy conversation. He hoped it would inspire agricultural businesses across the state to gain energy independence and diversify their revenue while keeping land in production.Why the grid pressure from data centres makes farm-based power a policy question for VirginiaThe council said Virginia’s electrical grid is at a breaking point. Rapid growth in data centres is driving demand, and it warned that the state may need to double or possibly triple its grid over the next 15 years or face recurring blackouts. As a land conservation organisation, it said it advocates clean energy solutions that respect natural resources and the rural economy.Donor support allowed the pilot to go ahead, and the United States Department of Energy’s National Lab of the Rockies provided technical assistance.You use AI every day. articles.title: Sarah Huckabee Sanders accuses 'The View' host of twisting her words in immigration exchange
articles.summary: Sarah Huckabee Sanders accused Ana Navarro of twisting her words on "The View" while defending Trump's border security and his recent comments on "60 Minutes."
articles.body: Arkansas Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders accused "The View" co-host Ana Navarro of twisting her words as she praised President Donald Trump for securing the border during Monday's show. Navarro noted that the president said during an interview with "60 Minutes" on Sunday that he might have been "too tough" on immigration, and asked Sanders, "I'm wondering if you agree with him, and if he actually believes that? How do you reconcile elevating Stephen Miller, the architect of some of the most draconian immigration policies that we saw in Trump 1 when you were there, and now in Trump 2, including family separations and the Muslim travel ban? How do those two things go together? Make it make sense, because it makes no sense to me." Sanders, who served as Trump's second press secretary during his first term, said, "I think the first thing is the president was exactly right to secure our border and to put an intense focus on violent, criminal illegals. I think that was the right place. I think it needed to happen–" "I have to stop you there because the majority of the people that are being detained and deported do not have violent criminal convictions," Navarro interjected. VANCE SPARS WITH LIBERAL CO-HOSTS OVER IMMIGRATION ON 'THE VIEW' Sanders argued that wasn't what she said. "You're not going to twist my words around. What I said was the president was right to focus on those people. I think we have to have a secure border, and I think he did that. At the same time, I think he is right to be reflective and say there were certain people we shouldn't have cracked down on," Sanders added. During an interview with "60 Minutes" on Sunday, Trump told CBS' Ross Douthat that his immigration policy may have been "too tough." TRUMP DHS HITS 16 STRAIGHT MONTHS WITH 0 RELEASES AT THE BORDER "I think it both helped and hurt," Trump answered. "I think I got an A-plus for closing up the border… I get very high marks for getting the bad ones out." However, Trump acknowledged that many illegal immigrants living in the country were "good" people, a point he suggested had contributed to criticism of his immigration policies. "But I get hurt because we also took people that had good jobs, that — that created one violation, or breaking of the law, and that was that they came into the country illegally. Now, there is a large part of the country that think that they should be put out. And there's a large part of the country that think that they should be allowed to stay if they're good people working in a landscaping company, or working in a hotel, or doing something, right? And in some cases, paying taxes. And there's a large group of people [who] think that they should be allowed to stay," Trump said. The White House did not immediately return Fox News Digital's request for comment. Sanders recounted the death of an Arkansas pediatric nurse who she said was killed by an illegal immigrant in a drunk-driving crash. TRUMP’S SPECIAL STRATEGY TO DEPORT ILLEGALS GIVES HIM ANOTHER TOOL FOR ENFORCEMENT "There was a woman, Jennifer Ann Morton. She's a pediatric nurse in my state. She should be alive today if it had not been for an illegal immigrant that killed her on her way to work because they were driving drunk," she said. "That shouldn't have happened. That person was deported during Trump 1, came back under the Biden administration, and now she is no longer living in my state taking care of some of the most vulnerable children in our state." Co-host Sunny Hostin pushed back, "What about the 97% of those that [Trump] deported that did nothing criminal?" A Migration Policy Institute fact sheet from October said that 20% of the Trump administration's deportations in the first 18 months of his second term involved individuals with a criminal conviction. Sanders said that the president was right to reflect on some of his policies and called for comprehensive immigration reform. She approved of his handling of the border. And for her to blame Trump for trying to clean up the Biden administration’s mess is 31 flavors of unintentional comedy."

articles.title: Judge sets 2028 trial date for man accused of killing Charlie Kirk
articles.summary: The Utah judge said he would reserve 105 court days for Tyler Robinson’s trial. Jury selection will begin June 21, 2028.
articles.body: Tyler Robinson, the man accused of assassinating conservative activist Charlie Kirk, is scheduled to stand trial in the summer of 2028, Utah District Court Judge Tony Graf ruled Monday afternoon. Jury selection will begin June 21, 2028, Graf said. Robinson, 23, pleaded not guilty to aggravated murder and six related offenses in last year’s killing of Kirk, who was shot as he spoke to a crowd of several thousand people at Utah Valley University. At the urging of his family, Robinson turned himself in a day after the shooting. He could be eligible for the death penalty if convicted. The court will hold monthly pretrial status conferences to ensure constitutional rights for both Robinson and Kirk’s wife, Erika. The timeline is intended “to ensure that the constitutional rights of Mr. Robinson and Mrs. Kirk are upheld at every junction, each party is treated with the dignity and respect they are due, as they are human beings, and that the Sixth Amendment right is protected,” Graf wrote in his order. The Sixth Amendment guarantees the right to a speedy trial. “Given Mr. Robinson’s current status, unnecessary delay remains a serious concern,” Graf said, adding that he will reserve 105 court days for trial. In explaining the court’s timeline, Graf said both sides must have sufficient time to review tens of thousands of files of evidence, which includes 8 million digital artifacts and about 3.3 terabytes of data. Similarly, Graf said jury and setting selection must proceed at a pace that allows for thorough vetting. Utah County prosecutors said they expected a 17-week trial; they said they would be ready by October 2027, The Associated Press reported. But rather than hold the proceedings during the Thanksgiving and Christmas holidays, they initially proposed the trial begin Jan. 31, 2028. Robinson’s defense attorneys asked for a 2029 trial to give them time to prepare their case, but attorneys for Kirk’s widow pushed back against the defense’s proposed schedule, calling it “absurd” and suggesting that Robinson’s legal team was simply trying to delay. At the end of the hearing Monday, attorney Jeffrey Neiman said the family would accept the June 21 trial date but implored the court to hold to the schedule and avoid any further delays. “Look, the Kirk family obviously has the right to speedy disposition of this case. A trial in the summer of 2028, three years after Charlie’s assassination, does not feel very speedy to the Kirk family.” “The family has waited long enough already,” Neiman added. “They should not have to wait any longer for this.”

articles.title: FBI is investigating a possible homicide on a cruise ship that left Texas
articles.summary: MSC Cruises said the Seascape was told to return to the Port of Galveston after a “guest incident aboard our ship.”
articles.body: A suspect was taken into custody Monday in connection with an alleged homicide on a cruise ship that had docked in Galveston, Texas, federal authorities said Monday. The death was on the MSC Seascape, a 1,060-foot cruise ship that left Texas on Sunday but was instructed to turn around after what the cruise ship company described in a statement as a “guest incident aboard our ship.” In a separate statement, the FBI said it would not identify the suspect until the victim’s family was notified. The victim was also not identified. The agency described its investigation as ongoing and declined to provide additional details. The Galveston Medical Examiner’s Office said Monday that the deceased was a female and that an autopsy is scheduled for Tuesday. Becsei György, a passenger on the Seascape, told NBC News that a shipwide announcement was made around 10 p.m. Sunday that said, “Mike Echo at level 10.” György awoke Monday morning and was surprised to find that the ship had returned to Galveston. Outside, he said, he saw law enforcement and Border Patrol vehicles, as well as a person being escorted off the ship in handcuffs. It wasn’t immediately clear whether that person was the suspect. The FBI is primarily responsible for investigating homicides, assaults and other serious crimes on cruise ships that are within U.S. jurisdiction at sea. It said it is coordinating with the Coast Guard, Customs and Border Protection, port police and the cruise company. A spokesperson for MSC Cruises said that it is cooperating fully with the investigation and that the ship has since left Galveston and resumed its itinerary. According to Cruise Mapper, a cruise ship tracker, the Seascape was on a seven-night trip with stops on Mexico’s Yucatán Peninsula and Roatán, Honduras.

articles.title: Lead investigator for Dallas County Public Defender’s Office charged in stabbing death of his wife
articles.summary: Jimmy Spurger, who spent years investigating capital murder cases, remained in custody Monday.
articles.body: The lead investigator in the Dallas County Public Defender’s Office, who spent years investigating capital murder cases, was charged in the stabbing death of his wife. He remained in custody Monday. Jimmy Spurger, 54, was ordered held on $150,000 bond on a charge of murder after his arrest Friday in the death of Maria Spurger, 53, according to Dallas County Jail records and a police news release. According to an arrest warrant affidavit in the case, a request was made to Dallas Fire Rescue for a welfare check call at the couple’s apartment in Dallas. When no one answered the door after several knocks, Dallas Fire Rescue forced open the apartment’s door but had to clear furniture blocking the front door to be able to fully open it, according to the affidavit. “DFR found Complainant Maria Spurger who was unresponsive and lying on the couch with what appeared to be a knife lodged in her neck,” the affidavit states. The responders then found Jimmy Spurger sitting on the bed in the bedroom, but he did not respond to their questions about his well-being, the document states. They left the apartment and called police, who later found Maria Spurger covered in blood on the couch, the affidavit states. Police found a small knife next to Jimmy Spurger and multiple blood-covered, empty pill bottles in the kitchen, according to the affidavit. The police investigation determined Maria Spurger had been stabbed by “a known suspect,” a police statement said. Spurger was taken to the hospital and was unable to be immediately interviewed because of the many pills he had ingested, the affidavit states. Clay Jenkins, the county judge and its chief elected official, said on social media that he had ordered Spurger suspended. The Dallas County Public Defender’s Office said it was deeply saddened by the death. “Our thoughts and prayers are with her family and friends during this unimaginably difficult time,” it said. Dallas County court records show Jimmy Spurger had petitioned for divorce last month. The couple were married 35 years. Spurger had been in his position as investigative division supervisor for 11 months and worked with the Dallas County Public Defender’s Office for more than 13 years, according to his biography on the public defender’s website. The biography had been removed as of Monday. The majority of his time with the office was in the capital murder division, “where he conducted fact and mitigation investigations for some of the most complex and serious criminal cases handled by the office,” the biography states. It further said his experience includes investigating guilt-innocence issues and developing mitigation evidence. He spent more than 20 years in law enforcement, specializing in homicide investigations and crimes against persons, according to the biography. He also served with the Dallas County District Attorney’s Office in the child abuse and family violence division, the biography states. articles.title: Saudi Arabia reports new attack on key East-West pipeline
articles.summary: The oil pipeline runs through the desert to the coast and is essential for bypassing the Strait of Hormuz.
articles.body:
Saudi Arabia’s critical East-West oil pipeline has suffered another attack, according to state media.

An official at the Saudi Ministry of Energy said that the pipeline was targeted in the Medina region in the west of the country on Monday, causing a “limited fire” that was extinguished, the Saudi Press Agency reported.

“No injuries or fatalities were reported, and pipeline operations were unaffected,” it said.

The report did not identify the party behind the attack, but fighting continues to intensify between Saudi Arabia and the Yemeni government coalition that it backs, and the Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen.

The pipeline is essential for bypassing the Strait of Hormuz, which remains tightly constricted by the US-Israel war on Iran. It has come under attack several times as the war on Iran fuels a global energy crisis .

The Houthis have also repeatedly targeted Saudi oil infrastructure, including refineries and storage facilities, with drones and missiles.

The 1,200km (745-mile) pipeline runs through the desert across the Arabian Peninsula. It was shut down for several days in September after drone attacks, which Saudi Arabia said were launched from Iraq.

Since the conflict disrupted oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz, Riyadh has rerouted about 4 million barrels per day of crude via the East-West pipeline to Yanbu, equivalent to about 4 percent of global supply.

articles.title: Pope meets with clergy abuse survivors in Argentina
articles.summary: During private meetings with survivors, Pope Leo XIV pledged to reinforce safeguards and listen to victims.
articles.body:
Pope Leo XIV has met with five survivors of clerical sexual abuse on the second day of his historic visit to Argentina.

The private meetings in Buenos Aires on Monday were the first of several talks the pope is planning to hold with abuse survivors during his 12-day tour of Latin America, according to the Vatican.

“The Pope spoke individually with each of them, listened to their words and to the painful stories of their experiences, as well as to their proposals for strengthening paths towards healing within the Church,” the Vatican said in a statement.

The closed-door meetings followed a historic open-air mass that drew an estimated 2.5 million people to Avenida del Libertador, a major boulevard in the capital, at the Monumento de los Espanoles. It was the country’s first papal liturgy in nearly 40 years.

The meetings with survivors respond to the pope’s desire to “express his closeness to those who have suffered”, build paths to healing and ensure the church is a safe and “spiritually healthy” place, the Holy See Press Office said in October.

Leo, the first pope born in the United States, has consistently met with survivors during foreign visits as part of a wider outreach aiming to repair global relations and restore the Catholic Church’s credibility. Lawsuits, widespread sexual abuse and cover-ups have sullied its reputation over the last three decades.

While clergy abuse cases are difficult to track globally, a 2021 independent inquiry found there were an estimated 216,000 victims of the French Catholic Church’s clergy alone between 1950 and 2020. Earlier research found more than 10,600 people were abused by Catholic priests in the US between 1950 and 2002, while Australia counted 6,875 victims of Catholic clergy, religious and lay church workers between 1980 and 2015, according to a 2019 German study .

During the meeting, which lasted more than an hour, Leo, 71, listened to victims’ testimonies and reiterated his pledge to strengthen safeguarding in the Catholic Church. Before being named pope, Leo served as president of the Pontifical Commission for Latin America.

Argentina is the second stop on Leo’s three-country tour, which began in Uruguay and will wrap up in Peru.

His visit was the first by a pontiff since Pope John Paul II’s trip in 1987.

articles.title: Paul McCartney bought a remote 183-acre Scottish farm in 1966 to escape Beatlemania; he later expanded the land and found inspiration for 'Mull of Kintyre'
articles.summary: Sir Paul McCartney's Scottish farm has remained one of the most personal places in his life, far removed from the crowds and attention that surrounded his
articles.body: Sir Paul McCartney's Scottish farm has remained one of the most personal places in his life, far removed from the crowds and attention that surrounded his rise with The Beatles. Purchased in 1966, High Park Farm on the Kintyre peninsula offered the musician a chance to find peace in the countryside. What began as a modest rural property with 183 acres gradually grew into a much larger estate. Beyond providing privacy, the landscape also played a role in his musical journey, inspiring one of Wings' most memorable songs, Mull of Kintyre.Why Paul McCartney bought his Scottish farm in 1966McCartney purchased High Park Farm in June 1966, at a time when Beatlemania had made ordinary privacy difficult to find. According to House & Garden, the property was located on the Kintyre peninsula, not far from Campbeltown, and came with a three-bedroom farmhouse and 183 acres of land.The purchase came shortly after McCartney moved into his London townhouse at Cavendish Avenue. While the London residence placed him closer to the music industry's centre, the Scottish farm offered something entirely different. It was a private countryside get away where he could get away from the limelight of fans and reporters.For a musician whose everyday life had become increasingly public, the rural setting offered a valuable alternative. The property was not immediately ready for comfortable family living. House & Garden notes that the farmhouse was largely dilapidated when McCartney acquired it, with renovations beginning in 1969 after he married Linda Eastman.The McCartney family transformed the Scottish retreatThe farm became considerably more meaningful after McCartney married Linda in 1969. According to House & Garden, the couple began renovating High Park Farm that year, turning a neglected property into a place where they could spend time away from the demands of their careers.HELLO magazine reports that McCartney subsequently expanded his holdings around the original farmhouse. He purchased another nearby farm and added approximately 400 acres of land during the following years. House & Garden placed the additional acquisitions in 1970 and early 1971.The expansion also reflected the family's growing attachment to the area. Rather than treating Scotland simply as an occasional holiday destination, McCartney and Linda increasingly made it part of their family life.Their connection with the countryside became particularly important as they raised their children. The landscape offered opportunities for outdoor activities and a more relaxed environment.What made the Kintyre landscape so important to McCartneyMcCartney's relationship with Scotland was influenced by more than the practical advantages of owning a secluded property. House & Garden recounts his explanation in a 2021 interview, when he said John Lennon had helped inspire his interest in the Highlands.Lennon had visited relatives who owned a croft in the region and spoke enthusiastically about its scenery. Those descriptions left McCartney interested in the possibility of owning a Scottish property himself.However, it was Linda who helped him appreciate the landscape more deeply. In the interview cited by House & Garden, McCartney explained that spending time there with Linda and raising their family allowed him to experience the countryside in ways he had not previously understood.The farm eventually became associated with some of the most memorable music of his post-Beatles career.The farm that inspired Mull of Kintyre and was deeply connected to LindaOne of the most enduring connections between High Park Farm and McCartney's musical career is Mull of Kintyre, the song he co-wrote with Wings bandmate Denny Laine.The song was written as a tribute to the peninsula where the Scottish farm was located. It was about the landscape and it had a personal quality to the composition, a reflection of McCartney's affection for the region rather than another commercial recording.HELLO magazine identifies the farm as the place where McCartney and Laine created the song, which became Wings' biggest British hit. Released in 1977, Mull of Kintyre reached Christmas number one in the UK. House & Garden reports that the single sold more than two million copies, making it a major success for the band. The achievement gave the remote Scottish property an unexpected place in popular music history.Linda McCartney died from breast cancer in 1998, but the Scottish property continued to hold significance for her husband. articles.title: After meeting Qatar PM, Trump calls Iran war ‘effectively over’ militarily
articles.summary: Iranian officials dismissed Trump’s remarks as ‘fake news’ after he suggested keeping the ‘status quo’.
articles.body:
United States President Donald Trump has signalled that he considers the US-Israel war on Iran “effectively” at an end, after meeting Qatar’s prime minister in Washington, DC.

In a surprise briefing on Monday, Trump reiterated his position that the US had destroyed Iran’s military. But his remarks suggested he faces pressure from allies in the Middle East to bring hostilities to a close.

“Iran militarily is effectively over,” he said. “We’re just keeping it the status quo, and we’re doing that really at the behest of countries that are their neighbours.”

His comments followed a closed-door meeting with US Vice President JD Vance and Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani, who hailed the progress in a post on social media.

“We discussed the situation in the region and ways to progress the US-Iran talks,” the prime minister said. “Grateful for the positive discussions on reaching a deal and bringing peace to the region.”

Still, Trump acknowledged the “status quo” would involve continuing the US naval blockade against Iranian ports, as well as the newly announced Task Force Iron Gate, which seeks to cut off trade by land and through the Caspian Sea.

“Qatar, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait and others would prefer the status quo, that we remain as is,” he said. “In other words, a continuation of the greatest naval blockade in the history of our country. Probably in the history of the world.”

Trump also indicated in his briefing that the US was willing to resume fighting, should the need arise.

“Taking military action doesn’t seem to be a very necessary thing, but we’re locked and loaded, ready to go for any reason that changes,” he said.

“Israel and the entire Middle East are protected from Iranian danger and threats, and we’re seeing momentum toward the end of this conflict. I think it’s going to be ending fairly soon.”

Iranian officials, meanwhile, dismissed Trump’s latest remarks as a distraction.

“The war on Iran has already wrecked the US government. But Washington flails like a desperate gambler,” Iran’s Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei wrote in a post on social media.

“FOLD YOUR HAND. STOP manufacturing FAKE NEWS about imaginary talks.”

Separately, Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian said that the country’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei had called for an end to the situation, which he described as “neither war nor peace”.

Pezeshkian added that Iran was open to further negotiations but would not be coerced, according to Iranian media. “We will not surrender to force and bullying,” he said.

Since the war on Iran began on February 28, the conflict has spilled into surrounding countries and roiled international trade.

Almost as soon as the US and Israel began their attacks, Iran moved to shut down the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway for oil, gas and fertiliser, among other goods.

Iran also responded to US and Israeli strikes with missile and drone fire on its neighbours in the Gulf, including Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait and the UAE, with many of the attacks targeting US military installations.

Other, related conflicts have since emerged. Saudi Arabia has renewed its fight against the Iran-backed Houthis, and Israel began its occupation of southern Lebanon, as well as deadly air strikes.

In the nearly nine months since the war began, the US offensive against Iran has grown sporadic, with intermittent exchanges of fire.

In recent days, for instance, the Trump administration announced “minor strikes” against Iran’s Qeshm Island.

It also offered a $20m reward for “information about Iran’s nuclear program, including its facilities, equipment, and associated personnel”.

After the Twelve-Day War in June 2025, Trump had claimed that Iran’s uranium enrichment programme had been obliterated. But he has since made curtailing Iran’s nuclear programme a central premise for the ongoing war.

Iran has long denied seeking a nuclear weapon, maintaining its uranium enrichment programme is for the purposes of civilian energy generation.

Officials in Iran, meanwhile, have pushed for the US to accept seven conditions in order to end the war.

They include lifting US sanctions, releasing frozen Iranian funds, recognising a new shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz worked out with Oman, and ending the war on all fronts, including Israel’s attacks on Lebanon.

Qatar has served as one of several key mediators in the conflict. Sheikh Mohammed, the prime minister, also serves as foreign minister and has been known to act as an intermediary between Washington and Tehran.

In Monday’s closed-door meeting, he reportedly presented Trump with a two-day proposal from Iran to end the war.

Afterwards, reporters asked Trump in the briefing room, “Why not just declare an end to the conflict and be done with it?”

Trump replied by framing the continued US blockade as a question of regional security. He also called for a “long-term solution”, rather than a short-term one.

“We have some great allies there, and we have to make sure they’re not hurt, and they would be hurt,” he said.

“They are right now a lot safer than they were six months ago because Iran’s been very much decapitated. But they’re still the bully of the Middle East a little bit.”

articles.title: NHS boss received nearly £400,000 'redundancy' pay-off when she retired
articles.summary: The payment comes ahead of a planned major overhaul of Scotland's NHS which could see the number of health boards cut dramatically.
articles.body:
An NHS executive has received a near £400,000 redundancy pay-off after retiring from a health board, new figures show.

Following a 44-year career in the health service, Mary Morgan retired as chief executive of NHS National Services Scotland (NSS) in May.

But it has now been revealed Morgan received a £378,000 payment "under contractual redundancy terms" as part of an exit that came after NHS NSS was merged into a new quango called Public Services Delivery (PSD) Scotland in April.

A PSD Scotland spokesperson said Morgan retired after an "exceptional career" and all payments were in accordance with the terms and conditions of her employment.

The payment comes ahead of a planned major overhaul of Scotland's NHS which could see the number of health boards cut dramatically.

Swinney to cut number of health boards from 14 to two

Doctors say radical plan to merge Scotland's health boards should be scrapped

PSD Scotland started operating in in April and was set up to drive changes across the health and care system, and the wider public sector.

It replaced both NHS NSS and another quango called NHS Education for Scotland, whose chief executive Prof Karen Reid is now in charge of PSD Scotland.

Morgan, who earned between £160,000 and £165,000 a year, had been chief executive of NHS NSS since 2021.

BBC Scotland asked NHS NSS on 10 March what would happen with Morgan now her role was defunct.

The health board said the senior NHS executive was "considering her options and next opportunity in line with national workforce policies".

After a follow-up query three weeks later, Keith Redpath, the then chairman of NHS NSS, replied: "Mary Morgan retires on 3 May, concluding an exceptional 44-year career in NHS Scotland."

The NHS NSS accounts for 2025/26 show Morgan retired under contractual redundancy terms from PSD Scotland on 3 May and received a related amount of £378,000.

The same accounts show Morgan's pension pot, known as The Cash Equivalent Transfer Value, is just over £2m.

A PSD Scotland spokesperson said: "Mary Morgan retired on 3 May, concluding an exceptional 44-year career in NHS Scotland. All payment received was in accordance to the terms and conditions of her employment."

The BBC has approached Morgan, but she declined to comment.

articles.title: US Supreme Court allows border wall in Big Bend National Park to proceed
articles.summary: Lawsuit had sought to block border wall construction in national park by targeting waivers that sidestep protections.
articles.body:
The United States Supreme Court has allowed President Donald Trump’s administration to build a border wall through a remote section of Big Bend National Park in West Texas.

In its decision on Monday, the court granted the government’s emergency request to lift a lower court’s injunction that had paused construction while the matter was litigated.

The injunction, it said, “impedes the Government from advancing its ‘compelling interests’ in border security and integrity”.

The border wall has long been a signature part of Trump’s platform to restrict immigration into the US.

During his first successful bid for the presidency in 2016, for instance, he rallied supporters with chants of “Build the wall!”

But the push to expand the border barrier through the popular national park has met pushback from conservationists, local officials and some members of Trump’s own Republican Party.

Big Bend National Park includes mountain ranges and desert that serve as a home to endangered species like the Mexican long-nosed bat.

Opponents say the plan to build the wall through the park would disrupt the ecologically and culturally significant landscape.

The Trump administration, however, has depicted the project as an urgent priority for national security and immigration control. It has described the Big Bend area as an artery for irregular border crossings and drug trafficking.

US District Judge Kathleen Cardone blocked the construction in October, noting that while the Big Bend sector makes up more than 25 percent of the US-Mexico border, it accounts for only 0.3 to 2.2 percent of migrant apprehensions.

“Therefore, if the Big Bend Sector is an area of high illegal entry, so is every other sector, and the waiver authority would apply to the entire US-Mexico border,” Cardone wrote.

The Supreme Court, however, said the government was “exceedingly likely to prevail” on its argument that Cardone lacked jurisdiction under the 1996 Illegal Immigration Reform and Immigrant Responsibility Act, which limits the ability of lower courts to rule on border barriers.

Under that law, district courts can only hear claims alleging a violation of the US Constitution. The Supreme Court found that the challengers’ claim did not qualify, writing that “there is no such thing as a ‘constitutional’ major-questions claim”.

Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson was the only justice to indicate she would have denied the government’s request. She did not explain her reasoning.

The Center for Biological Diversity was among the plaintiffs who brought the lawsuit against the Department of Homeland Security, along with Friends of the Ruidosa Church and a local river guide and landowner.

The lawsuit challenged waivers used by the agency to fast-track border construction and sidestep environmental and conservation laws.

Without those waivers, plaintiffs said that construction would have to comply with laws such as the Endangered Species Act, the National Environmental Policy Act and the National Historic Preservation Act to alter the landscape in “one of the most remote and ecologically and culturally significant landscapes in the United States”.

articles.title: Judge dismisses case from Dolly Parton’s manager alleging her nephew threatened her estate
articles.summary: The manager of the late beloved country singer’s estate asked for a dismissal last week after the two sides came to an agreement.
articles.body: A Tennessee judge on Monday dismissed a case brought by Dolly Parton’s longtime manager, who was seeking an injunction against her nephew and head of security, alleging he had threatened her estate and its employees. The manager, Danny Nozell, asked for the dismissal Thursday after the two sides came to an agreement. The order from Chancellor I’Ashea L. Myles finalizes that request without prejudice, meaning it can be filed again. Nozell, who runs She’s Alive, an entity founded to manage and protect Parton’s estate, had secured a temporary restraining order against Bryan Seaver and his security company, Squadron Augmented Protection Services, in September. The complaint seeking the temporary restraining order said Seaver had threatened violence and the destruction of Parton’s legacy and business empire. Nozell wanted to turn the order into a permanent injunction against Seaver. The two sides were to have publicly argued the claims on Tuesday. Seaver’s lawyers said in a statement Monday that he “cares deeply about his Aunt Dolly, her music, her family, and the legacy she left behind.” “He has made a career out of protecting his aunt while she was alive and remains committed to Dolly and his family,” the statement said. “Mr. Seaver is grateful to put this misunderstanding behind him so that the entire family can continue to grieve peacefully and ensure that the bright light of Dolly’s legacy remains completely untouched.” The dismissal brings a sudden and quiet end to a serious rift in the beloved country superstar’s inner circle that began while she was sick with cancer and spilled into public view in the weeks after her Aug. 25 death. Neither side nor court documents have revealed anything about why the complaint was withdrawn, though one court filing said the sides had reached an agreement. Emails requesting details and comment were sent to lawyers for Nozell and She’s Alive. Seaver, whom Parton handpicked to announce her death, said in court filings that he considered Nozell a close friend and ally before the restraining order and said the text messages Nozell cited as evidence of his threats were a “private conversation between two friends who were both frustrated, grieving and discussing strategy.” Parton was a widely adored singer, songwriter, philanthropist and country music icon who rose from a log cabin in the Tennessee mountains to a stardom that spanned generations with songs including “Jolene,” “Coat of Many Colors,” “9 to 5” and “I Will Always Love You.” She also left behind a business empire, much of it based in her hometown, that employed many of her close friends and family.

articles.body:
Ações itinerantes reforçam a importância do diagnóstico precoce e da quebra de preconceitos na rotina masculina — Foto: Arquivo Secom

A Prefeitura de Macaé realizou uma série de ações de conscientização voltadas ao Novembro Azul, com foco na prevenção, nos cuidados preventivos e no diagnóstico precoce de enfermidades. A iniciativa foi conduzida pela equipe do Programa Saúde do Homem, vinculada à Gerência de Vigilância em Saúde da Secretaria Municipal de Saúde, que percorreu diferentes pontos da cidade, incluindo setores instalados no Centro Administrativo Luiz Osório (Cealo), o Mercado Municipal de Peixes e a Colônia dos Pescadores.

Durante as abordagens, os profissionais dialogaram diretamente com os trabalhadores sobre a importância de manter exames e consultas em dia, tratando de temas como a prevenção do câncer de próstata, combate ao tabagismo e ao alcoolismo, prática de atividades físicas, alimentação balanceada e saúde mental. O trabalho buscou ainda desconstruir tabus culturais que frequentemente afastam o público masculino das unidades de saúde.

Rede municipal oferece exames e acompanhamento contínuo para prevenção de doenças crônicas e urológicas — Foto: Arquivo Secom

A equipe do programa destacou que o autocuidado deve ser inserido na rotina diária e não pode ser secundarizado pelas responsabilidades profissionais. A orientação técnica adota como método os pilares formados por nutrição adequada, rotina de exercícios físicos, sono reparador e propósito de vida com bem-estar emocional, enfatizando que a preservação da saúde precisa ser tratada como prioridade pelo homem.

Além do alerta para o câncer de próstata — cujos procedimentos avaliativos na rede municipal incluem o exame de sangue PSA (Antígeno Prostático Específico) e o toque retal conforme histórico e faixa etária —, a mobilização chamou atenção para dados epidemiológicos. Segundo o Boletim de Produção Ambulatorial, Macaé registrou cerca de 4.385 atendimentos ligados à prevenção e ao tratamento do câncer de próstata entre janeiro de 2020 e julho de 2024.

O cuidado integral abrange ainda a vigilância contra doenças cardiovasculares, tais como hipertensão arterial, insuficiência cardíaca e infarto, além de debates abertos sobre a saúde sexual e reprodutiva, abrangendo o tratamento de disfunções e a prevenção de Infecções Sexualmente Transmissíveis (ISTs). Outro ponto enfatizado pela Secretaria Municipal de Saúde foi a relevância da saúde mental diante de sobrecargas emocionais e financeiras do cotidiano.

A campanha incentiva também a participação ativa masculina no planejamento familiar e no acompanhamento do pré-natal das parceiras, momento estratégico para que o próprio homem realize exames de rotina, testes rápidos e atualização da caderneta de vacinação, exercendo a paternidade responsável desde a gestação.

Orientações e cuidados essenciais da campanha:

Realizar acompanhamento médico periódico e exames preventivos (PSA e toque retal conforme avaliação clínica)

Manter controle contínuo da pressão arterial e hábitos que reduzam o risco de doenças cardiovasculares

Adotar alimentação saudável, praticar atividades físicas e evitar o uso de tabaco e excesso de bebidas alcoólicas

Procurar acolhimento médico para cuidados com a saúde mental e sexual sem receio ou constrangimento

Participar ativamente das consultas de pré-natal da companheira e manter a vacinação atualizada

Três trabalhadores terceirizados morreram asfixiados em uma fábrica da Tata Electronics no sul da Índia que produz peças para iPhones da Apple, disse uma fonte nesta terça-feira (20).

Os três morreram durante um trabalho de manutenção em um tanque de água na unidade localizada em Hosur, no estado de Tamil Nadu, segundo a fonte, que tinha conhecimento direto do caso. O jornal New Indian Express informou que as mortes ocorreram na segunda-feira.

articles.title: Felipe Diogo: Júri julga acusado de matar jogador com 10 tiros | G1
articles.standfirst: Foragido, Kleber Archangelo dos Santos responde por homicídio triplamente qualificado pela morte de Felipe Diogo, ex-jogador do São Bernardo, em outubro de 2023. Júri estava marcado para agosto, mas foi adiado por causa de ausência de testemunha.
articles.summary: O julgamento de Kleber Archangelo dos Santos analisa o assassinato do atleta Felipe Diogo, atingido por dez disparos durante uma confusão em Ribeirão Preto em 2023.
articles.body:
A Justiça de Ribeirão Preto (SP) marcou para esta terça-feira (10) o júri popular de Kleber Archangelo dos Santos, foragido e acusado de matar com dez tiros o jogador de futebol Felipe Diogo, em outubro de 2023.

O tribunal do júri tinha sido marcado para agosto, mas acabou adiado devido à ausência de uma testemunha. A sessão está marcada para começar às 10h no Fórum de Ribeirão Preto.

A expectativa é de que cinco testemunhas de defesa e cinco de acusação sejam ouvidas. A participação do réu não foi confirmada.

Santos, que deve ser levado ao júri, segundo sua defesa, responde por homicídio qualificado por motivo fútil, meio cruel e recurso que dificultou a defesa da vítima.

O réu é tio da ex-namorada de Felipe e atirou na vítima durante uma confusão envolvendo a família da jovem e o atleta, segundo o Ministério Público. Ele teve a prisão preventiva decretada em novembro de 2023, mas nunca foi preso.

Kleber Archangelo dos Santos, acusado de matar jogador de futebol em Ribeirão Preto (SP). — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

Advogado de defesa de Santos, Daniel Rondi disse que o réu tem direito a não participar do julgamento.

Ele afirmou que seu cliente recebeu ameaças e decidiu não se apresentar mesmo com o mandado de prisão em aberto. Ele argumenta que o réu matou o jogador para defender a sobrinha.

"A defesa trará esses argumentos, demonstrará que naquele momento o meio foi o meio necessário para impedir que uma outra morte acontecesse, a morte de uma mulher que poderia ser vítima de feminicídio naquele mesmo dia."

Felipe Diogo, conhecido como Felipe Favela, foi morto a tiros em Ribeirão Preto (SP) em outubro de 2023 — Foto: Redes sociais

O jogador de futebol, conhecido como Felipe Favela, tinha 21 anos e era atacante do São Bernardo, mas passava férias com a família em Ribeirão Preto, onde foi atingido por ao menos dez disparos em 31 de outubro de 2023.

Segundo o promotor de Justiça Marcos Túlio Nicolino, do total de disparos, cinco foram nas costas.

Felipe chegou a ser socorrido por moradores e levado à Unidade de Pronto Atendimento (UPA) Norte, mas não resistiu.

No dia em que morreu, Felipe tinha ido até a casa onde vivia com a ex, na Rua Tabatinga, no Jardim Jandaia, Zona Norte da cidade.

Em carta, Kleber Archanjo dos Santos, acusado de matar jogador de futebol em Ribeirão Preto, SP, disse que vai comparecer a júri — Foto: Reprodução/g1

Na época, a família da jovem alegou que ela tinha registrado um boletim de ocorrência contra Felipe por agressão. Durante a investigação, o Ministério Público não identificou qualquer apuração em andamento ou queixa contra o jogador.

Segundo a mãe do jogador, no dia do homicídio, o filho ligou por volta das 19h pedindo que ela fosse até a casa dele.

Ao chegar ao local, ela disse ter visto Kleber Santos na janela do imóvel, armado com um revólver. Ela conta que pediu para que a família da ex-nora explicasse o que estava acontecendo. Ainda segundo a testemunha, apesar dos pedidos, Santos atirou na sequência.

Felipe Diogo com a filha caçula no colo em Ribeirão Preto, SP — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

articles.title: Vale-refeição e alimentação: Justiça mantém regra para trabalhador | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão provisória restaurou norma anterior sobre taxas de operação e prazo de repasse do dinheiro. Regra que ampliou aceitação dos cartões nas 'maquininhas' foi mantida.
articles.summary: A Justiça Federal suspendeu taxas e prazos das novas regras do vale-refeição e alimentação, mas manteve a aceitação de todas as bandeiras de cartões nas maquininhas.
articles.body:
A Justiça Federal no Distrito Federal suspendeu, nesta segunda-feira (9), parte das novas regras que começaram a valer no sábado (7) para os cartões de vale-alimentação e refeição .

A decisão é liminar (provisória) e vale apenas para as empresas vinculadas à Associação Brasileira das Empresas de Benefícios ao Trabalhador (ABBT).

A lista inclui as maiores firmas do ramo, como Alelo, Pluxee, VR e ValeShop.

💳 O principal benefício das novas regras para o trabalhador, no entanto, foi mantido: a chamada interoperabilidade.

Pelo novo modelo, uma maquininha de cartão que aceita vale-refeição ou vale-alimentação terá que aceitar todas as "bandeiras". Ou seja: o trabalhador não precisará mais perguntar se o local aceita aquele cartão específico.

➡️ O governo reconhece que pode haver falhas pontuais durante a implementação do novo sistema. Veja aqui o que fazer se o estabelecimento aceitar vales diversos, mas recusar o seu .

Novas regras de vale-refeição e alimentação ampliam operadoras aceitas em maquininhas — Foto: Jornal Nacional

🔎 Na prática, a medida busca resolver um problema comum: chegar a um restaurante, supermercado ou lanchonete e descobrir que o local aceita vale-refeição ou vale-alimentação, mas não a bandeira do seu cartão.

A liminar desta segunda-feira é assinada pelo juiz federal Frederico Botelho de Barros Viana e vale até que a Justiça Federal no DF tome uma decisão definitiva sobre o tema. Não há data para que isso aconteça, e o governo federal pode recorrer.

Na ação, a associação das empresas de benefícios questionou uma série de mudanças estabelecidas pelo decreto em 2025 – e que entraram em vigor neste sábado.

a migração obrigatória de determinadas operadoras para arranjos abertos – em que firmas diferentes podem atuar nas diversas etapas do cartão (emissão, prospecção da rede credenciada, operação financeira, etc);

a imposição de limites às taxas cobradas pelas emissoras de

a redução do prazo para repasse dos valores aos estabelecimentos.

O juiz federal determinou que, nesses casos, o regime anterior do Programa de Alimentação do Trabalhador (PAT) seja mantido para essas empresas até um julgamento definitivo da ação.

✍️ Ou seja: as regras alteradas pela decisão tratam da relação entre as diferentes empresas envolvidas no funcionamento dos vales-refeição e alimentação. E não, da relação do trabalhador com essas empresas.

Em nota ( íntegra abaixo ), a ABBT afirmou que a decisão "abre um caminho para os ajustes necessários à regulamentação do Programa de Alimentação do Trabalhador (PAT), preservando os aspectos relevantes para a evolução do programa".

O g1 entrou em contato com a União e aguardava retorno até a última atualização desta reportagem.

A decisão suspende para as associadas à ABBT, entre outros pontos:

a obrigação de operadoras com mais de 500 mil trabalhadores migrarem para arranjos abertos;

o teto de 3,6% para a taxa de desconto (MDR);

o teto de 2% para a tarifa de intercâmbio;

o prazo máximo de 15 dias para o repasse dos valores aos estabelecimentos;

os prazos de adequação às novas exigências;

competências dadas ao Comitê Gestor para modificar taxas, prazos e regras dos arranjos de pagamento.

A decisão também determina que a União e o Ministério do Trabalho e Emprego se abstenham de aplicar penalidades às empresas beneficiadas pela liminar com base nos dispositivos suspensos.

A União deverá ser citada para apresentar sua defesa. O processo também será encaminhado ao Ministério Público Federal (MPF).

O Programa de Alimentação do Trabalhador (PAT) foi criado em 1976 com o objetivo de melhorar as condições de alimentação e nutrição dos trabalhadores, especialmente os de baixa renda.

Administrado pelo Ministério do Trabalho e Emprego, o programa estabelece regras para empresas que oferecem benefícios de alimentação aos funcionários, inclusive por meio de vale-refeição (VR) e vale-alimentação (VA).

A adesão dos empregadores ao programa é voluntária. As empresas participantes que cumprem as exigências podem ter acesso ao tratamento tributário e aos incentivos fiscais previstos na legislação.

As mudanças mais recentes foram estabelecidas pelo Decreto nº 12.712/2025. As novas regras começaram a entrar em vigor neste sábado (7).

Leia abaixo a íntegra da nota da Associação Brasileira das Empresas de Benefícios ao Trabalhador (ABBT):

A Associação Brasileira das Empresas de Benefícios ao Trabalhador (ABBT) entende que a decisão liminar da 22ª Vara Federal Cível do Distrito Federal abre um caminho para os ajustes necessários à regulamentação do Programa de Alimentação do Trabalhador (PAT), preservando os aspectos relevantes para a evolução do programa.

Para a ABBT, o momento permite avançar na discussão sobre o aprimoramento do PAT, com segurança jurídica, previsibilidade e avaliação dos impactos das mudanças sobre todo o ecossistema. A entidade defende regras claras, tecnicamente fundamentadas e que considerem a sustentabilidade operacional do setor e a finalidade social do programa.

A ABBT reafirma sua disposição de manter o diálogo com o governo e os demais atores do setor, contribuindo para a construção de soluções regulatórias que favoreçam a evolução do PAT e preservem seu papel na promoção do acesso dos trabalhadores brasileiros à alimentação adequada.

articles.title: Emissões fósseis podem cair em 2026, mas queda é incerta; entenda | G1
articles.standfirst: Relatório projeta recuo de 0,4% nas emissões de CO2 de carvão, petróleo e gás. Queda do petróleo e avanço da energia limpa puxam resultado, mas total global ainda deve aumentar.
articles.summary: Relatório projeta recuo de 0,4% nas emissões de CO2 de carvão, petróleo e gás. Queda do petróleo e avanço da energia limpa puxam resultado, mas total global ainda deve aumentar.
articles.body:
Emissões de gases do efeito estufa podem provocar aquecimento maior do que o previsto, apontam novas evidências. — Foto: AFP

As emissões globais de dióxido de carbono (CO2) provocadas pelo uso de carvão, petróleo e gás natural podem registrar uma pequena queda em 2026, aponta a nova edição do Orçamento Global de Carbono , relatório anual que acompanha quanto CO2 o mundo emite e quanto é absorvido por florestas e oceanos.

A projeção central aponta para um recuo de 0,4% em relação a 2025, o que levaria as emissões fósseis a 38,2 bilhões de toneladas neste ano.

Mas o resultado ainda é incerto. A margem calculada pelos pesquisadores vai de uma queda de 1,5% a uma alta de 0,6%.

Ou seja, os dados apontam para uma redução, mas ainda não permitem afirmar que 2026 terminará definitivamente abaixo do ano passado .

A maior mudança vem do petróleo. As emissões desse combustível devem cair 1,9%, em parte por causa do choque no mercado de energia provocado pela guerra no Irã.

O gás natural também deve registrar uma pequena queda, de 0,3%. Já o carvão segue na direção contrária, com alta projetada de 0,6%.

📉 ENTENDA: uma queda em apenas um ano não significa que as emissões globais entraram definitivamente em trajetória de redução. Recuos também ocorreram durante crises como a pandemia e a crise financeira de 2008 e foram seguidos por novas altas. Para frear o aquecimento global, a redução precisa ser contínua e duradoura.

Os próprios autores fazem essa ressalva.

"Uma queda nas emissões em um único ano não é um pico, a menos que seja impulsionada por mudança estrutural", afirma Glen Peters, pesquisador do Cicero e um dos autores do levantamento.

Parte da redução prevista também está ligada ao avanço da energia solar, eólica e dos veículos elétricos.

Pela primeira vez, os pesquisadores estimaram diretamente quanto essas tecnologias estão evitando de novas emissões.

Em 2026, seriam cerca de 500 milhões de toneladas de CO2, o equivalente a aproximadamente dois terços das emissões adicionais que seriam provocadas pelo crescimento da demanda mundial por energia.

Ainda assim, uma possível queda dos combustíveis fósseis não significa que o planeta emitirá menos CO2 no total neste ano.

Isso porque as emissões associadas a mudanças no uso da terra, como desmatamento e degradação de florestas, devem aumentar. Com isso, o total global deve passar de 42,8 bilhões de toneladas em 2025 para 43,3 bilhões em 2026 .

“Os números relativamente favoráveis mostrados neste ano pelas emissões de CO2 de origem fóssil foram, em parte, afetados por acontecimentos geopolíticos que reduziram sensivelmente as emissões. Por isso, é preciso cautela ao quantificar as tendências observadas”, afirma Ernesto Rodríguez Camino, presidente da Associação Meteorológica Espanhola, em comentário divulgado pelo Science Media Centre España (SMC España).

“O aumento da demanda mundial de energia ainda não é compensado pela implantação de fontes renováveis para geração de eletricidade e pela mobilidade elétrica”, diz Camino. “A implantação de energias limpas precisa acelerar para que seja possível controlar as emissões de CO2.”

É justamente nesse ponto que o Brasil aparece com destaque. Na média entre 2016 e 2025, o país foi o maior emissor líquido de CO2 do mundo por mudanças no uso da terra, respondendo sozinho por 28% do total global , com cerca de 1,37 bilhão de toneladas por ano .

Emissões em trajetória de aumento — Foto: Arte/g1

A Indonésia aparece em seguida, com 14,3%, e a República Democrática do Congo, com 11,4%. Juntos, os três países respondem por mais da metade das emissões líquidas globais desse tipo.

O Brasil também retira uma quantidade significativa de carbono da atmosfera com o crescimento e a recuperação de florestas. Mesmo assim, segundo o levantamento, essa absorção ainda é superada pelas emissões do desmatamento.

Já quando entram na conta apenas carvão, petróleo e gás, o peso brasileiro é bem menor: o país respondeu por cerca de 1,3% das emissões fósseis globais em 2025.

Mesmo com sinais de desaceleração em parte das emissões, o levantamento mostra que resta pouco espaço para cumprir a meta mais ambiciosa do Acordo de Paris.

Os pesquisadores estimam que o mundo ainda pode emitir cerca de 150 bilhões de toneladas de CO2 para manter uma chance de 50% de limitar o aquecimento global a 1,5°C acima dos níveis pré-industriais. No ritmo atual, isso equivale a menos de quatro anos de emissões.

“Embora apareçam tendências ligeiramente positivas, o esforço global coletivo para reduzir as emissões deveria acelerar para cumprir os limites de aumento da temperatura global estabelecidos no Acordo de Paris”, afirma Camino.
