articles.standfirst: Apostas podem ser feitas até as 20h em lotéricas ou pela internet.
articles.summary: Apostas podem ser feitas até as 20h em lotéricas ou pela internet.
articles.body:
O concurso 3.084 da Mega-Sena pode pagar um prêmio de R$ 3,5 milhões para os apostadores que acertarem as seis dezenas. O sorteio ocorre às 21h desta terça-feira (10), em São Paulo.

No concurso do último domingo (8), nenhuma aposta acertou a faixa principal e o valor acumulou.

O g1 transmite todos os sorteios das Loterias Caixa, ao vivo . A transmissão começa momentos antes de cada dia de concursos, no site e no canal do g1 no YouTube .

A aposta mínima para a Mega-Sena custa R$ 6 e pode ser realizada também pela internet – saiba como fazer a sua aposta online .

Volante da Mega-Sena — Foto: Ana Marin/g1

As apostas podem ser realizadas até as 20h (horário de Brasília) em qualquer lotérica do país ou por meio do site e aplicativo Loterias Caixa, disponíveis em smartphones, computadores e outros dispositivos.

Já os bolões digitais poderão ser comprados até as 20h30, exclusivamente pelo portal Loterias Online e pelo aplicativo.

Ainda segundo a Caixa, para os sorteios realizados aos domingos as apostas simples podem ser efetuadas até as 22h de sábado por meio das unidades lotéricas, pelo Portal Loterias Caixa e do aplicativo Loterias Caixa.

A comercialização dos Bolões Caixa nos canais eletrônicos, nesse caso, acontece até às 10h45 do domingo, quinze minutos antes da realização dos sorteios.

O pagamento da aposta online pode ser realizado via PIX, cartão de crédito ou pelo internet banking, para correntistas da Caixa. É preciso ter 18 anos ou mais para participar.

A probabilidade de vencer em cada concurso varia de acordo com o número de dezenas jogadas e do tipo de aposta realizada. Para um jogo simples, com apenas seis dezenas, que custa R$ 6, a probabilidade de ganhar o prêmio milionário é de 1 em 50.063.860, segundo a Caixa.

Já para uma aposta com 20 dezenas (limite máximo), com o preço de R$ 232.560,00, a probabilidade de acertar o prêmio é de 1 em 1.292, ainda de acordo com a instituição.

articles.title: Secretário de Guerra de Trump é alvo de pedido de impeachment: veja as 8 acusações apresentadas contra Hegseth | G1
articles.standfirst: Deputado republicano acusa Pete Hegseth de manter guerras sem autorização do Congresso, enfraquecer a proteção de civis e autorizar mortes em operações militares. Trump e Marco Rubio criticaram o pedido e defenderam a atuação do secretário.
articles.summary: Deputado republicano acusa Pete Hegseth de manter guerras sem autorização do Congresso, enfraquecer a proteção de civis e autorizar mortes em operações militares.
articles.body:
Deputado Thomas Massie e o secretário de Guerra, Pete Hegseth — Foto: Evelyn Hockstein/Reuters; Kevin Lamarque/Reuters

O deputado republicano Thomas Massie, do estado de Kentucky, apresentou um pedido de impeachment na segunda-feira (9) contra secretário de Guerra dos Estados Unidos, Pete Hegseth. No documento, Massie expõe oito motivos que o levaram a fazer o pedido.

Para o republicano, o secretário violou leis que limitam os poderes do presidente e do governo americano para iniciar e manter operações militares.

A resolução apresentada à Câmara dos Representantes (equivalente a Câmara dos Deputados no Brasil) inclui a condução da guerra contra o Irã sem autorização do Congresso, mortes de civis em operações militares e ataques contra embarcações suspeitas de transportar drogas.

No documento, Massie afirma que Hegseth abusou dos poderes do cargo e desrespeitou a Constituição americana ao executar e manter operações militares sem a autorização exigida por lei .

O deputado também acusa o secretário de enfraquecer mecanismos de proteção a civis durante conflitos , autorizar mortes extrajudiciais e retaliar um senador por críticas à atuação das Forças Armadas.

O principal argumento do republicano é que o governo Trump não poderia decidir sozinho quando iniciar uma guerra, por quanto tempo mantê-la ou quando encerrar operações militares sem respeitar os limites estabelecidos pelo Congresso.

Guerra contra o Irã é a maior reclamação de Massie

A primeira parte da resolução trata justamente da guerra contra o Irã, iniciada em 28 de fevereiro desse ano.

Massie argumenta que o Congresso não declarou guerra ao país nem aprovou uma autorização específica para o uso de forças militares americanas no conflito.

Segundo ele, também não havia uma emergência nacional provocada por um ataque iraniano aos Estados Unidos que justificasse uma ação militar sem autorização prévia dos parlamentares.

O deputado cita a Lei de Poderes de Guerra , aprovada em 1973, que estabelece limites para o envolvimento das Forças Armadas americanas em conflitos sem autorização do Congresso.

A legislação determina que o presidente deve retirar as tropas de operações militares em até 60 dias, caso os parlamentares não declarem guerra, não autorizem especificamente o uso da força ou não aprovem uma prorrogação do prazo.

Pela lei, existe ainda a possibilidade de uma extensão de até 30 dias , desde que o presidente apresente uma justificativa por escrito de que a permanência das tropas é necessária para garantir a segurança dos militares durante a retirada.

A ordem exata dos acontecimentos foi a seguinte:

Massie afirma que Trump comunicou o Congresso sobre o início das operações no Irã em 2 de março , mas não obteve autorização para continuar o conflito .

Segundo o deputado, o prazo de 60 dias terminou em 1º de maio, e o período adicional de 30 dias, mesmo que fosse considerado válido, terminou em 1º de junho . Entretanto, Trump não enviou a certificação necessária para justificar essa prorrogação.

Apesar disso, Hegseth teria continuado a autorizar e manter as operações militares. Para Massie, o secretário ignorou os limites legais e permitiu que o governo decidisse unilateralmente pela continuidade de uma guerra.

O deputado também cita uma resolução aprovada pelas duas Casas do Congresso em junho desse ano, que determinava a retirada das tropas americanas das operações não autorizadas no Irã.

Segundo o documento, Hegseth desrespeitou a decisão e manteve as ações militares.

Massie também acusa o secretário de Guerra de enfraquecer as estruturas responsáveis por evitar mortes de civis durante operações militares.

Nesse trecho, o republicano relaciona as decisões administrativas de Hegseth a um ataque americano contra uma escola primária na cidade de Minab, no Irã, que teria deixado mais de 200 mortos e feridos.

De acordo com a resolução, Hegseth teria desmontado mecanismos do Departamento de Defesa criados para avaliar riscos a civis e reduzir vítimas durante conflitos.

A interrupção de atividades de proteção a civis;

A retirada de mais de 90% dos funcionários que trabalhavam com o tema em comandos militares; e

O corte de recursos de um banco de dados usado pelo Exército para registrar e verificar denúncias de mortes de civis.

O deputado também afirma que Hegseth tentou acabar com exigências legais de proteção a civis, mas não conseguiu obter a aprovação do Congresso. Mesmo assim, segundo Massie, o secretário teria interrompido atividades relacionadas a essas garantias.

'Letalidade máxima, não legalidade moderada'

Outro ponto levantado é a retirada dos principais advogados militares do Exército, da Marinha e da Força Aérea. Esses profissionais são responsáveis por orientar os comandantes sobre a legalidade das operações . Para o republicano, a medida enfraqueceu a fiscalização jurídica dentro das Forças Armadas.

Massie também critica declarações públicas de Hegseth contra regras que limitam a atuação militar.

O secretário já havia defendido uma postura de maior letalidade nas operações, com a frase "letalidade máxima, não legalidade moderada". Para o deputado, esse discurso contribuiu para criar uma cultura dentro do Pentágono que desvaloriza as normas de proteção a civis.

➡️ Na avaliação de Massie, o enfraquecimento dessas estruturas contribuiu para o ataque à escola Shajareh Tayyebeh , em Minab .

O documento afirma que três mísseis americanos atingiram o prédio em 28 de fevereiro, quando havia estudantes no local . Segundo a resolução, pelo menos 156 civis morreram , incluindo ao menos 120 crianças , e outras dezenas ficaram feridas.

O parlamentar argumenta que o episódio não foi apenas um erro isolado durante a guerra, mas consequência de decisões que teriam enfraquecido os mecanismos de verificação de alvos e prevenção de danos a civis.

Mortes em embarcações suspeitas de transportar drogas

EUA explodiram barco no Oceano Pacífico — Foto: Southcom

Outra acusação envolve operações militares americanas contra embarcações suspeitas de transportar drogas no mar do Caribe e no oceano Pacífico .

Massie afirma que Hegseth autorizou ataques que mataram pelo menos 221 pessoas em águas internacionais, sem que houvesse autorização do Congresso para o uso da força militar nesses casos.

Foram realizados pelo menos 63 ataques contra 67 embarcações desde setembro de 2025. O deputado argumenta que suspeitas de tráfico de drogas deveriam ser tratadas por meio de operações de fiscalização, apreensão e prisão, e não com ataques militares que resultam na morte dos ocupantes.

Massie também acusa Hegseth de permitir ataques contra sobreviventes de embarcações atingidas e de não organizar operações de resgate adequadas .

Como exemplo, o republicano cita o primeiro ataque da campanha, em 2 de setembro de 2025. Uma embarcação com 11 pessoas foi atingida e virou. Cerca de 45 minutos depois, dois sobreviventes que ainda estavam presos aos destroços foram mortos em um segundo ataque.

Em outro episódio, em dezembro de 2025, oito pessoas sobreviveram inicialmente a ataques contra embarcações no Pacífico, mas morreram no mar antes da chegada das equipes de resgate, que só apareceram cerca de 45 horas depois.

Para Massie, as operações substituíram procedimentos policiais de abordagem e prisão pelo uso de força letal , sem que os suspeitos tivessem sido julgados ou que houvesse comprovação de que representavam uma ameaça militar.

Retaliação contra senador e captura de Maduro

Ditador deposto da Venezuela Nicolás Maduro algemado por agentes do Departamento Antinarcóticos após descer de helicóptero em Nova York em janeiro de 2026, após ser capturado pelos EUA. — Foto: REUTERS/Adam Gray/File Photo

A resolução também acusa Hegseth de tentar intimidar o senador democrata Mark Kelly , ex-capitão da Marinha, após ele publicar um vídeo em novembro de 2025 dirigido a integrantes das Forças Armadas .

Na gravação, Kelly afirmou que militares podem se recusar a cumprir ordens ilegais. A declaração fazia referência às operações contra embarcações suspeitas de transportar drogas.

Segundo Massie, o Departamento de Defesa ameaçou convocar Kelly novamente para o serviço militar e submetê-lo a um julgamento militar. Em janeiro de 2026, Hegseth também teria emitido uma censura formal contra o senador, com ameaças de processo criminal e outras punições caso ele continuasse criticando as operações militares.

Para o deputado, as medidas representaram uma tentativa de punir um integrante do Congresso por exercer seu direito de expressão e fiscalizar as ações do governo.

Outro artigo do pedido trata da operação americana que resultou na captura do então presidente venezuelano Nicolás Maduro e de sua mulher, Cilia Flores , em 3 de janeiro de 2026.

Massie afirma que a operação, batizada de Absolute Resolve , representou um ato de guerra contra um país soberano, realizado sem declaração de guerra ou autorização específica do Congresso .

O deputado também sustenta que a ação foi apresentada sob a justificativa de combate ao narcotráfico, mas teria outros objetivos, como permitir que os Estados Unidos assumissem o controle das reservas de petróleo venezuelanas.

O documento ainda acusa Hegseth de ter dirigido operações militares no Iêmen em 2025 que resultaram na morte de aproximadamente 224 civis e entre 500 e 600 combatentes houthis . Massie argumenta que os ataques ocorreram sem autorização do Congresso e sem uma ameaça iminente aos Estados Unidos que justificasse a ofensiva.

O pedido de impeachment foi criticado pelo presidente Donald Trump , que saiu em defesa de Hegseth nesta segunda-feira (9).

Em entrevista à agência Reuters, Trump minimizou as acusações e atribuiu as críticas ao secretário aos resultados das operações militares americanas.

"Ele é culpado de duas coisas, basicamente: vencer duas guerras", afirmou o presidente, em referência à guerra contra o Irã e à operação que capturou Maduro na Venezuela.

Hegseth, por sua vez, classificou as críticas como motivadas politicamente e afirmou que não está preocupado com a pressão. O secretário também defendeu a ofensiva contra o Irã

A guerra contra o Irã provocou uma disparada nos preços dos combustíveis, nas passagens aéreas e na inflação geral. O aumento dos custos afetou o orçamento das famílias americanas e se tornou um dos fatores de insatisfação com o governo Trump . Uma pesquisa da Associated Press apontou que cerca de seis em cada dez eleitores americanos consideraram errada a decisão de realizar operações militares contra o Irã.

O deputado americano Thomas Massie (republicano do Kentucky) concede entrevista coletiva sobre sua proposta de impeachment do secretário de Defesa, Pete Hegseth, no Capitólio, em Washington, nos Estados Unidos, em 9 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: Reuters/Evelyn Hockstein

articles.title: NI education: School meals price rises for second time in a year
articles.summary: The price of a school dinner in a primary school will have risen from £2.60 to £3.40 since the start of 2026.
articles.body:
A headteacher said she believes "families are going to struggle" as the price of school dinners is to go up for the second time in a year.

The price of meals for pre-school, primary and special school pupils will go up by 30p, for post-primary pupils will they will rise by 15%. It follows an increase of just under 20% introduced by the Education Authority (EA) in January 2026 .

Áine Leslie, principal of Malone Integrated College in Belfast, said this will put further pressure on families who are already worried about the cost of living crisis.

But the EA said that the amount parents would have to pay was still well below the average cost of producing a school meal, estimated at over £5.20.

The latest increase means that the price of a paid for school dinner in a primary school or special school, for instance, will have risen from £2.60 to £3.40 since the start of 2026.

Pupils eligible for free school meals will not be affected.

The rise in school dinner prices is not the only measure introduced by the EA in response to what they describe as "an exceptionally challenging financial position".

There will also be a change to some menus in schools, replacing baked desserts with cheaper alternatives.

At Malone Integrated College about 55% of pupils have free school meal entitlement and there are also a lot of parents who are on lower incomes.

When the prices of school meals increased earlier this year, Leslie said she remembers "sitting with the head of the cafeteria and heartbreakingly decide how much to put up each item".

"I think the cumulative effect of this will be immense, particularly families who have multiple children, both at a primary school and a post-primary school, and trying to make ends meet, it's going to become incredibly difficult," Leslie told BBC News NI.

"I can't imagine what it would be like for families trying to budget that moving forward, as well as planning for Christmas.

"I firmly believe families are going to struggle at Malone.

"I do believe that there will be some families and some young people who will be worried about the stigma attached to this, and won't voice their concerns and won't ask for help. And as an integrated school, that's really sad for us.

She added: "I think it's going to be quite cutthroat for families.

"Already, we have some of our children, particularly in junior school talking about Christmas and how they've had discussions with their families that things are going to be much more scaled down this Christmas, just with the general cost of living crisis.

"And then this is only going to amplify the situation even more for young people."

Leslie added that not having a healthy, balanced diet or going without food will be a "barrier to learning".

Christos Gaitatzis is the principal of Omagh High and described the increase of 15% on a school meal as "excessive".

"What is the price index at the moment – is it 3,4, 5%? I would imagine that would be the reasonable increase that you would put on anything, so they are going three times the value - to me it is unreasonable," he told BBC News NI

Close to 30% of pupils at his school are on free school meals.

"You would expect that the cost for a child every week, when a price of a meal is close to £5, we are talking about £20 a week, £100 a month – that's a significant cost for lunch," Gaitatzis said.

"So other measures have to be taken by the families in order to make savings, for example pack lunches – then would that diet be balanced?

"We're talking about a society where the importance of nutrition provided by schools has significant impact on your mental and physical health, so you effectively deter these families and children having these nutritious meals by putting the price up.

"Clearly this will have an overall future impact on the health of the kids."

Northern Ireland's commissioner for children and young people said he was ''flabbergasted" at the change.

Chris Quinn said what makes the move "particularly difficult to accept is that it comes shortly after schools were directed towards energy-saving guidance advising people who were cold to wear more clothes rather than turn up the thermostat ".

"I strongly advised the Education Authority to remove that guidance and made clear that responsibility for financial pressures in education should not be transferred to children and families."

The commissioner added: "Children did not create the financial crisis in education and they should not be expected to pay the price for it.

"School meals are not a luxury. For many children they are an essential part of the school day, and these increases will hit hardest those families already struggling with the cost of living."

Payments to schools for school milk are at risk.

The EA currently pays milk subsidies to around 500 schools.

The Authority is to seek funding from the Department of Agriculture, Environment and Rural Affairs (Daera).

The EA are also planning to offer more parents payments to transport their children to school rather than paying for a taxi to do it.

At the minute, some parents receive parental payments if their children is eligible for free school transport but no private providers, like taxis, are available .

Charges for EA music lessons for pupils are also set to rise again, and some schemes run in schools will no longer be funded.

The Authority, however, has not specified what is at risk.

In a statement, the EA said that they "were being asked to deliver important services to children and young people with insufficient funding".

They said that they hoped to save £20m by introducing the measures on top of £30m saved this year.

They also said costs, such as providing energy for schools, continued to rise.

"These were difficult decisions which sought to balance our commitment to children and young people alongside the requirement to live within the funding allocated for the year," the EA said.

"We are also mindful of the pressures across all public services in NI and of the fact that any overspend this year may impact on next year's finances."

The Northern Ireland Executive has yet to agree a budget amid a dispute with the secretary of state about how Northern Ireland is funded .

articles.title: Ukraine peace talks resume in Abu Dhabi after months-long pause
articles.summary: Kyiv, Washington and Moscow are all sending delegation to the United Arab Emirates for the first trilateral talks since February.
articles.body:
Moscow and Kyiv are privately showing "a little bit of flexibility" on the issue of who would controls Ukraine's eastern regions in a postwar scenario, US officials have said.

The comments came on the eve of the first trilateral talks aimed at ending the war in Ukraine since February.

Senior officials from Moscow, Kyiv and Washington will meet in Abu Dhabi as the fifth anniversary of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine approaches.

Jared Kushner - Donald Trump's son-in-law and part of the US delegation alongside peace envoy Steve Witkoff - said the talks would be focused on addressing the "postwar security concerns" of both Russia and Ukraine.

"An important part of this process is encouraging all parties to begin thinking seriously about what comes after the war," Kushner wrote on X.

But Moscow and Kyiv's positions on ending the conflict in the first place remain far apart.

A key area of disagreement between the two involves Ukraine's eastern region of Donetsk, which is by now mostly occupied by Russia.

Moscow has demanded that Ukraine relinquish the parts of Donetsk which it still holds, while Kyiv wants to freeze the contact line to maintain control over those sections, which it says are crucial to its future security.

While neither side has budged on these demands, the US official speaking on the eve of the talks suggested that this was just the public stance and that Moscow and Kyiv had shown "a little bit of flexibility, privately".

However, he acknowledged that the issue would not be solved without discussions about a new "security architecture".

"They will not solve the Donetsk issue and the territorial issue until they know what the security architecture is going to be after the war," the official said. "And keep in mind, we're not going to be able to finalise one without the other."

For Ukraine, a post-war "security architecture" may include reassurance that allies will come to its aid if it's attacked again. For Russia, that could be its longstanding ambition to see Nato roll back from eastern Europe – which would be alarming to Europeans.

The framework being proposed includes security consultations and crisis communications hotlines, as well as "reciprocal de-escalation measures" between the two. The officials also floated the re-activation of the Nato-Russia Council that has been largely paused since 2022.

The last round of trilateral talks, held in Geneva in February, ended without a breakthrough. Soon after, the US-Israel war on Iran diverted Washington's attention from Ukraine, and no other discussions were held since.

Since then, European leaders - who have been largely excluded from peace talks – have pushed to be involved in the process amid concerns that decisions about the security of their continent would be made without them.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen urged on Monday to include Nato allies and EU members into any "meaningful discussions about Europe's security architecture". President Volodymyr Zelensky has repeatedly stated Kyiv wanted Europe to be part of the talks.

The US official said the Americans would propose moving into a multilateral format bringing the Europeans into the discussion. "Hopefully we'll get the Russians on board," the official said, while acknowledging that "the Russians have a bad taste in their mouth with the Europeans."

Since the start of his second term in office, US President Donald Trump – who once boasted he could end the war in Ukraine within a day – has spearheaded several rounds of talks to end the conflict, albeit with little success.

Meanwhile, his increasingly conciliatory approach towards Moscow has fuelled deep unease in Kyiv and across the European Union.

After meeting Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev in Washington last week, Trump touted a forthcoming "big, beautiful agreement" on Ukraine which "might involve all of Europe".

Many in Ukraine are sceptical that this would result into a fair peace.

Ukrainian MP Oleksandr Merezhko, head of the foreign affairs parliamentary committee, told the BBC he believes Trump wants "a quick deal at the expense of Ukraine", which will certainly be rejected by Kyiv.

The only way to make Putin start real negotiations is by putting greater pressure on Russia through sanctions and deep strikes, Merezhko said.

"While Putin has a war machine up and running, he has no incentives to negotiate." He also mentioned recent moves by Trump, such as his deal to buy diesel from Russia, as something that "only encourages Moscow to continue the war".

Moscow's delegation in Abu Dhabi will include Kremlin aide Vladimir Medinsky, deputy foreign ministers Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin, spy chief Igor Kostyukov and army general Yury Zhigarlovsky.

Kyiv is sending several senior officials who have been part of previous negotiating teams, including Foreign Intelligence Service head Rustem Umerov, Volodymyr Zelensky's chief of staff Kyrylo Budanov, and MP Davyd Arakhamiya.

Away from Abu Dhabi, Russia continues to pummel Ukraine with deadly bombardments and strikes on energy infrastructure, viewed in Kyiv as proof Moscow wants to corner Ukraine into accepting a deal on Russia's terms.

On Monday, Kushner was cautious to point out that the Abu Dhabi talks could at most "build momentum toward the next phase of negotiations."

"This is an extraordinarily difficult and complicated conflict," he wrote on X, adding the US was "approaching these discussions with determination and realism."

articles.title: Charlamagne tha God calls out Dave Chappelle's Kirk comments, wouldn't wish them 'on my worst enemy'
articles.summary: Charlamagne Tha God said on "The Breakfast Club" that he doesn't "find the humor" in Dave Chappelle's joke about feeling "better" after Charlie Kirk's assassination.
articles.body: Radio host Charlamagne tha God criticized comedian Dave Chappelle's joke about the assassination of Turning Point USA (TPUSA) founder Charlie Kirk on Monday. Despite rules barring cell phones from the Madison Square Garden show, a video circulating on social media on Friday showed Chappelle appearing to make the remarks during his "Karmageddon" tour stop in New York City. "I feel f----- up saying this. It’s scary being a public speaker. And I mean, look, ever since that guy, Charlie Kirk, got murdered, and I shouldn’t say this publicly, but, I feel better," Chappelle said. 'SNL' WEEKEND UPDATE ANCHOR CALLS REPUBLICANS SLURS, MOCKS CHARLIE KIRK IN STAND-UP SPECIAL After playing the audio of his comments on his radio show "The Breakfast Club," Charlamagne immediately responded that he didn't "find the humor" in the comment. "I don't find the humor in people getting clapped, okay?" Charlamagne said. "Any of us can be shot, and I don't want anybody getting shot because somebody disagrees with their opinion. So yeah, you have the freedom to, you know, joke and talk about whatever you want to joke and talk about, but personally I don't want to deal with the energy of that. Like I don't wish stuff like that on my worst enemy." WELCH DOUBLES DOWN ON TPUSA FEUD, CALLS GROUP 'LOSERS' AFTER LAUGHING AT JOKE ABOUT KILLING CHARLIE KIRK AGAIN Some of his co-hosts noted that the clip of Chappelle's comments was released without any additional context. Charlamagne agreed but remarked that it seemed like it was an "observation" made by Chappelle. "It just sounded like he made an observation — at least from what that clip just played, that it was just like he felt better after Charlie Kirk got shot and killed," Charlamagne said. PETE DAVIDSON SPARKS BACKLASH AFTER EXPLICIT JOKE ABOUT SLAIN CHARLIE KIRK DURING NETFLIX ROAST Fox News Digital reached out to Charlamagne's and Chappelle's representatives for comment. In his comments, Chappelle described not only feeling "better" after Kirk's death but also experiencing unexpected high spirits after the news. "I just be driving around like, ‘Why am I in such a good mood? Oh!'" Chappelle remarked. Chappelle received backlash across social media for what some commentators called a "sick" joke. In response to the viral video, TPUSA pointed Fox News Digital to Erika Kirk's statement on X, in which she wrote that treating the destruction of human life as a punchline is "disgusting." "A culture that laughs at assassination is one of profound moral decay. It threatens the very foundation of our country and the principles that hold our democracy together. You do not have to agree with someone’s politics to recognize the value of their life. This should not be so hard," she wrote. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP In an interview with Fox News Digital, TPUSA spokesperson Andrew Kolvet made similar comments, acknowledging people's freedom of speech but encouraging a level of decorum. "We're not asking people to, you know, be evangelical Christians here. We're asking don't celebrate, condone or glorify political violence. Don't be happy when someone's assassinated. It's a very, very low bar. But if we don't keep it, then everything else falls apart," Kolvet said.

articles.title: 'Angels' singer Robbie Williams gives his $40 million Florida mansion a rock-star makeover with a 2,000-square-foot guest pavilion and a recording studio
articles.summary: British singer Robbie Williams is planning to add a 2,000-square-foot guest pavilion featuring a potential recording studio to his $40 million waterfront
articles.body: British singer Robbie Williams is planning to add a 2,000-square-foot guest pavilion featuring a potential recording studio to his $40 million waterfront mansion in Coral Gables, Florida. The singer purchased the estate in an off-market deal in 2025, with an additional $5 million for furnishings. The planned expansion, by Miami-based developer Manny Angelo Varas, is expected to add between 2,500 and 3,500 square feet to the property. The development will also include wellness and technology upgrades, while a floating padel court is being explored as another possible addition to the estate.How much did Robbie Williams pay for his $40 million Florida mansionWilliams purchased the waterfront estate in the exclusive Old Cutler Bay neighbourhood of Coral Gables, Florida, in an off-market deal reported at $40 million. According to The New York Post, the transaction also included an additional $5 million for furnishings. The purchase was expected to set a new record for the neighbourhood, with the property valued at approximately $5,000 per square foot.Built in 2016, the 19,380-square-foot smart home sits on a one-acre peninsula with 435 feet of water frontage, a 75-foot dock and views on three sides. The estate features seven bedrooms, seven full bathrooms and two powder rooms. Other existing amenities include a resort-style swimming pool and spa, a fire pit, an outdoor kitchen, an 18-car garage and a wine cellar.What will the 2,000-square-foot guest pavilion includeThe planned expansion will be overseen by Miami-based developer Manny Angelo Varas, who is known as "The Billionaire's Builder". According to the developer, the project involves new construction rather than simply renovating the existing interiors. Speaking to The New York Post, Varas said: "We're doing a ground-up build." He also explained that Williams would move into the existing property while construction work was underway.One of the main additions will be a 2,000-square-foot guest pavilion designed to serve multiple purposes. The space is being planned to accommodate a recording studio alongside other functional areas. Explaining the proposed use of the pavilion, Varas told the publication: "We're creating functional spaces that could be used as a recording studio and multiple different functions." He added that the arrangement would allow Williams to work from home when he was not on tour.How will wellness technology transform Robbie Williams' $40 million mansionThe guest pavilion forms part of a wider construction plan that is expected to add between 2,500 and 3,500 square feet to the property. Varas told The New York Post that the development would include additional functional spaces while retaining the home's existing design. The project is also expected to introduce wellness and technology upgrades throughout the estate.Among the planned improvements is an air-quality monitoring system. Varas explained that sensors would be installed within the air-conditioning system to monitor the indoor environment. "We're putting sensors within the AC to make sure we have a clean air environment throughout the entire home," he said. The developer also revealed that he was exploring the possibility of adding a floating padel court connected to the property, inspired by a similar facility in the Exumas.How did Drake's $75 million purchase lead to Robbie Williams' Florida moveWilliams' move to Florida follows the sale of his Beverly Hills estate to Canadian rapper Drake for $75 million. According to Varas, the decision to relocate from California was influenced by lifestyle, safety and tax considerations. The developer told The New York Post that the move was primarily about seeking a different environment, adding that he was also working with other clients relocating from California to the Miami area.The singer had initially considered purchasing Rosie O'Donnell's former property on Star Island, but structural concerns reportedly led to the cancellation of the contract. Varas explained that the house did not meet the current flood-code requirements, meaning it would effectively need to be demolished and rebuilt. He said the process could take between two and three years, prompting Williams to pursue the Coral Gables property instead. The sellers of the estate were The Real Housewives of Miami star Dr Nicole Martin and her husband, attorney Anthony Lopez, who had purchased it for approximately $21.5 million in 2022.The entire expansion project was expected to be completed in under a year, according to the July 2025 report. The proposed guest pavilion, recording studio, wellness upgrades and potential floating padel court form part of the plans for Williams' new Florida residence.Disclaimer: This article is based on information publicly available and reporting by The New York Post. The Times of India has not independently verified the property details, purchase price, renovation plans or transaction circumstances mentioned. The proposed construction, including the guest pavilion and recording studio, should not be interpreted as confirmation from Robbie Williams or his representatives.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: France blames Iran for cyberattacks on supermarket fridges, summons ambassador
articles.summary: French authorities on Monday accused Iran's Revolutionary Guards of orchestrating cyberattacks that disrupted commercial refrigerators and freezers across
articles.body: French authorities on Monday accused Iran's Revolutionary Guards of orchestrating cyberattacks that disrupted commercial refrigerators and freezers across the country, warning that Tehran of consequences.A joint report by French intelligence and cybersecurity agencies identified Shahid Kaveh, described as a cyber offensive unit linked to the Revolutionary Guards, as being behind the hacking campaign. It also named three alleged associates — Hamid Reza Lashgarian, Mahdi Lashgarian and Reza Salarvand, Reuters reported.French foreign minister Jean-Noël Barrot said the Iranian ambassador had been summoned to the foreign ministry. He also warned that the European Union could impose further sanctions on Iran over the attacks.The attacks targeted hundreds of French supermarkets in early October, disrupting cold-storage systems. The report said around 700 commercial establishments across France had been targeted, with at least 15 fires breaking out as hackers increased the temperature of refrigeration units.Most of the affected sites were supermarkets, although small butcher shops, a slaughterhouse and food-processing factories were also hit.Appeared as vigilante hacking groupsAccording to the French report, the hackers operated through several front organisations posing as vigilante hacking groups, including "CyberAveng3rs" and "Cyber Isnaad Front", Reuters reported.French investigators said they linked Shahid Kaveh to the attacks by examining the digital infrastructure used to sabotage refrigeration systems, comparing the intrusion patterns with other operations attributed to the unit and identifying traces of Persian language in the attack infrastructure.Paris prosecutors said separately that they had sought international arrest warrants for those allegedly responsible.Blood banks targetedThe October attacks were followed this month by another wave of hacking that affected more than 100 establishments across Europe. The latest incidents also disrupted refrigerators used by French blood banks, forcing staff to transfer some blood supplies to alternative cold-storage units.The attacks have been among the most disruptive cyber incidents linked to the conflict with Iran, which began in February. Other alleged digital disruptions during the conflict have included attacks on the Los Angeles transit system in March, US water treatment plants in July and ships bound for the United States in August.Government agencies and technology companies on both sides of the Atlantic have been investigating the incidents. Microsoft had privately linked Iran to the October cold-storage sabotage at least two weeks earlier, according to three people familiar with the matter. The company declined to comment.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: NTSB recovers cockpit voice recorder from Learjet crash site in Florida
articles.summary: The NTSB recovered the cockpit voice recorder from the Learjet 60 crash site near Greenacres, Florida, as investigators probe the cause of the incident.
articles.body: The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) announced on Monday that it has recovered the cockpit voice recorder (CVR) of the Learjet 60 that crashed last week near Greenacres, Florida, killing all nine people on board. "NTSB investigators have recovered the cockpit voice recorder (CVR) of the Learjet 60 that crashed on Nov. 1 near Greenacres, Florida," the NTSB said on X. The CVR was found at the location of the initial impact​, according to the NTSB. The NTSB said the CVR is being evaluated in the board's Vehicle Recorders Laboratory in Washington, D.C. TIMELINE OF LEARJET CRASH THAT KILLED AUSTIN FAMILY TRACES FINAL MINUTES FROM TAKEOFF TO FLORIDA PLUNGE The excavation work at the impact site has been completed. This comes after investigators said on Friday that they recovered part of an engine from the Learjet. Crews started excavating the site on Wednesday after utility workers had drained water and cleared other hazards, the NTSB said. Once investigators began digging, they found a part of one engine, the board said. Earlier last week, investigators recovered the left tail elevator, which controls the jet's pitch, in three separate pieces. One of them was found nearly four miles from where the Learjet 60 crashed. FLORIDA PLANE CRASH VICTIMS IDENTIFIED AFTER 9 PEOPLE KILLED IN FIERY WRECK "Even small pieces of the wreckage may contain important evidence that could help investigators determine what happened," the agency wrote last week on X. The Learjet 60 left Austin-Bergstrom International Airport around 10:37 a.m. on Sunday, bound for North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas. The aircraft plunged into the ground in Palm Beach County shortly before 1 p.m., killing everyone aboard. Austin tech entrepreneur Adam Robinson, 45, was killed in the crash alongside his wife, Helen Sharp, 40, their children, Emma, 4, and Charlie, 2, the children's nanny, Anita Maria Cetina, and couple Rachael Reed and Charmi Fehr. Heavy rain and thunderstorms were reported across South Florida when the Learjet crashed. Investigators said the weather will be a major focus of their probe. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP At about 41,000 feet, an air traffic controller told the flight crew that moderate precipitation was roughly five miles away and said they could move either left or right, stressing that the turn toward Freeport in the Bahamas "looks pretty bad." The crew was then instructed to fly to a waypoint near Naples, Florida. The crew made a deviation toward Palm Beach County and reported that weather conditions were deteriorating. The crew told air traffic control that there was icing and turbulence, asking the controller if there was a "better ride" ahead. Fox News' Adam Sabes contributed to this report.

articles.title: US-Iran war: Trump says more US attacks on Iran 'highly unlikely'
articles.summary: The president says the US is keeping "status quo" with Iran but remains “locked and loaded” should the situation in the Middle East change.
articles.body:
Donald Trump has said "Iran militarily is effectively over", and said that there is "positive momentum" behind negotiations to end the Middle East conflict.

"We're just keeping it the status quo," the US president said on Monday. "And we're doing that really at the behest of countries that are their neighbours."

Addressing reporters from the White House press briefing room, Trump said that renewed US attacks on Iran were "highly unlikely" but that the US was "locked and loaded" should the circumstances change.

Iranian officials have repeatedly expressed doubts about Trump's prior comments about resolving the conflict.

Responding to a question over why he would not officially declare an end to the war, Trump said that some of the Gulf allies could still face Iranian aggression.

"We have some great allies there and we have to make sure they're not hurt," he said, suggesting that the US naval blockade on Iranian ports was helping to make the region more secure.

This is not the first time that Trump has said the Iran war is "militarily" over, but the circumstances for him are different now.

The president has hinted at de-escalation in Iran after a bruising set of midterm election results for the Republicans last week, which senior figures including Vice-President JD Vance blamed on the Iran war.

Ahead of the midterms, Trump had said US forces conducted what he described as "minor strikes" on an Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz . However, in an interview with 60 Minutes that aired on Sunday, the president said that he did not currently see "any reason" to escalate the conflict.

Trump hosted Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdul Rahman Al Thani in the Oval Office earlier on Monday, saying they had an "excellent conversation" about negotiations to end the war.

In a post on X, the Qatari leader said he held "positive discussions" with Trump and Vance on "reaching a deal and bringing peace to the region".

Efforts to broker a peace between Washington and Tehran have largely been held indirectly through mediators since the war first broke out following joint US-Israeli strikes in February.

Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates are among the US's Gulf allies that have been hit by Iranian strikes over the course of the war, in addition to the threat of strikes that have led to major air travel disruptions in the region.

Post-election recriminations over the US war in Iran are already placing pressure on members of the Trump administration.

Republican congressman Thomas Massie launched a strong attack against Trump's Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on Monday over the war in Iran, requesting a vote in the House of Representatives to impeach him.

Trump has backed Hegseth, who says he is "not worried" about the looming impeachment threats, calling Massie's effort a "sham".

While the move is unlikely to succeed with Republicans still in control of Congress until January, Democrats have expressed willingness to impeach Hegseth once the new session begins and they have control of both the House and the Senate.

articles.title: Californians reject Prop 40 wealth tax for billionaires
articles.summary: Proposition 40 targeted Californian billionaires with a 5% tax on their total wealth, including assets such as shares as well as income.
articles.body:
California voters have voted to reject a wealth tax on its billionaires.

The ballot proposal would have levied a one-time tax on the state's mega wealthy to help fund healthcare. It took nearly a week of counting votes after the midterm election to determine a projection on the measure.

There are about 200 billionaires in the state, including Meta's Mark Zuckerberg , reality television star Kim Kardashian and media mogul Oprah Winfrey.

Proposition 40 targeted Californians with a wealth of more than $1.1bn (£800m) with a 5% tax on their total wealth, including assets such as shares as well as income. It failed amid divisions among Democrats and labour unions.

Are California voters about to impose 'world's first' tax on billionaires?

Had it passed, experts believe it would have been the world's first wealth tax targeting billionaires.

The tax would have raised about $100bn to make up for federal funding cuts to healthcare in California as a result of President Donald Trump's sweeping tax and spending bill.

Those who backed the measure had argued it would help ensure that the ultra-wealthy were contributing their fair share and helping backfill gaps in the state's budget.

The wealth tax faced fierce opposition, including from Google co-founder Sergey Brin, as well as California Governor Gavin Newsom and labour unions.

Newsom, whose tenure as governor is coming to an end, had expressed concerns that the measure could cause the wealthy to leave the state and drive out their crucial income tax revenue.

Some billionaire critics of the measure spent millions trying to crush it, with a handful even moving out of the state to evade the possible tax. Brin gave more than $100m to a political organisation funding ballot measures that could block the tax, according to the Los Angeles Times.

Dave Regan, head of the union that led the charge for the measure, said on election night that the billionaires' efforts to block the tax created "a lot of confusion and a lot of second-guessing among people who really in their hearts know what the right the thing to do is".

Regan, who is president of Service Employees International Union-United Healthcare Workers West, pledged to seek a billionaire tax once more in 2028.

The measure had odds stacked against it, with two other propositions on the ballot that would have effectively reversed it, even if it passed.

California, home to some 23 million registered voters, has the largest economy in the country and boasts the fourth largest global economy. It is home to one of the highest concentrations of billionaires in the world, but also has one of the highest wealth gaps.

articles.title: 'No intention to attack Europe': Russia rejects fears of military confrontation
articles.summary: Russia has no intention or plans to attack European countries and has no reason to do so, deputy foreign minister Sergei Ryabkov said on Monday, rejecting
articles.body: Russia has no intention or plans to attack European countries and has no reason to do so, deputy foreign minister Sergei Ryabkov said on Monday, rejecting Western discussions about a possible military conflict between Moscow and Europe.Speaking at a roundtable titled “Militarization of Europe: What Next?”, held under the auspices of the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE), Ryabkov said Western countries were discussing the prospect of a military confrontation as though it were “almost predetermined and inevitable”.According to a statement published on the Russian foreign ministry's website, Ryabkov said Moscow posed no threat to any country and had no plans to attack anyone in the near, medium or long term.However, he warned that Russia would be “forced to respond” if subjected to aggression.Russia calls for dialogue with European countriesRyabkov also accused some European governments of having no genuine intention of ending the Russia-Ukraine conflict. He said the conflict could have been resolved while taking into account the legitimate interests of all parties, but alleged that the West had pushed Ukraine to abandon reasonable solutions and choose war.On the future of relations between Moscow and European capitals, Ryabkov said Russia believed European countries would sooner or later be willing to resume dialogue on the basis of equality, indivisible security, pragmatism and mutual consideration of interests.He added that long-term stability in Europe could not be achieved without taking into account the interests of Russia and its allies.At the same event, Yulia Zhdanova, head of the Russian delegation to the Vienna Negotiations on Military Security and Arms Control, said European countries had offered their populations no vision of the future beyond the notion that conflict with Russia was inevitable.She also criticised Nato's concept of “escalation management”, describing it as harmful. Zhdanova said it was a mistake to believe that an escalation between Nato and Russia could be kept under control, arguing that the approach encouraged Nato and the European Union to act recklessly rather than reduce military risks.Russia-Ukraine negotiations set to resumeRyabkov's remarks came as Russian and Ukrainian officials prepared to hold two days of US-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi, their first negotiations since February.European powers, including France, Germany and the European Commission, were also expected to send officials, although Russia has opposed their participation in the negotiations.Ukraine's delegation head Rustem Umerov said on Monday that Kyiv was working to ensure Europe remained part of the diplomatic process. Ukrainian delegates were expected to meet European allies separately to brief them on the discussions.The Russian delegation will again be led by Kremlin aide Vladimir Medinsky. Ryabkov is also part of the team for the first time, alongside senior military officer Yuri Zhigarlovsky.The talks follow recent diplomatic efforts by US President Donald Trump, who has suggested that a broader agreement could end the conflict and potentially address Europe's security.However, Russia has continued to insist that Ukraine surrender the entire eastern region of Donbas before a peace deal, a demand Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has rejected.Zelenskyy said on Monday that Ukraine's recent battlefield performance, including the recapture of some territory in Donetsk, had strengthened its negotiating position. He also urged Washington to persuade Moscow to end the war.The negotiations are taking place amid disagreements over territorial concessions and security guarantees.A senior Ukrainian official told Reuters that Kyiv would not consider giving up territory, adding that the issue could be discussed only at a leaders' level and in the context of appropriate security guarantees.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Global capital for Sanatan pilgrimage': Akhilesh's big Ayodhya promise ahead of 2027 UP polls
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav made a vow to transform Ayodhya into the “global capital of Sanatan pilgrimage”, pledging transparent
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav made a vow to transform Ayodhya into the “global capital of Sanatan pilgrimage”, pledging transparent temple administration, world-class infrastructure and measures to revive the local economy ahead of his proposed visit to the Ram Temple on December 12.In a lengthy social media post, Yadav also accused the BJP of weakening the bond between Lord Ram and the Nishad community, promised to protect traditional boatmen and warned that those involved in alleged land and circle-rate scams in Ayodhya would face action if his party returned to power.“We are committed to restoring the honour and dignity of the city of Ayodhya,” Akhilesh said, alleging that the number of devotees and pilgrims visiting the temple town had been declining because of the hurt caused by the “theft of the Ram temple”. He said the decline had directly affected the local economy and promised to reverse the trend.“We will both improve and transform it. By introducing transparent administration at Ayodhya’s temple, we will also restore trust. By providing world-class infrastructure, we will make Ayodhya the ‘global capital of Sanatan pilgrimage’,” he said.The SP chief also promised measures to prevent the alleged mistreatment of poor people in the temple town, referring to an incident involving a woman and children collecting oil.“We will create an Ayodhya where no arrogant person can beat a poor woman or a boy or girl collecting oil and humiliate or oppress them,” he said.The SP chief further said that if voted to power, his government would provide oil and ghee through the public distribution system. “Once in government, we will also provide ‘oil and ghee’ in rations to meet the body’s nutritional needs,” he added.He further invoked the association between Lord Ram and Nishadraj, a central figure in the Ramayana tradition, and accused the BJP of attempting to undermine the relationship.“We will promote traditional boating in Ayodhya, so that traditional boatmen benefit from it and the deep bond between Lord Ram and Nishadraj can be restored,” he said.“The BJP wants to break this bond because BJP supremacists never want anyone to remember any scene of Lord Ram and the PDA community embracing one another,” Yadav added.PDA, or Pichhda, Dalit and Alpsankhyak (backward classes, Dalits and minorities), is the social coalition that the SP chief has been seeking to consolidate politically.Akhilesh also targeted alleged irregularities in land transactions and the circle rates in Ayodhya, promising scrutiny of land records and action against those responsible. “We will free Ayodhya from outside contractors and scrutinise land records. Outsiders are the ones who have looted Ayodhya,” he said.“No BJP leader or corrupt official involved in the massive circle-rate scam will escape. Their coffers, filled with the proceeds of Ayodhya’s plunder, will be emptied,” he added.The SP chief also called for legal action against people who insult religious deities and prominent figures, saying those who encourage such remarks should also be held accountable. “We will also create a system to ensure that no foul-mouthed person can insult the deities or great figures of any religion, let alone those of Lord Ram or Lord Krishna, or go about freely after doing so,” he said.Yadav further said that those encouraging people who make abusive remarks should also face consequences.“Those who encourage such wicked people who utter abusive words are also complicit in their sin, and they too will be punished appropriately for their involvement in a conspiracy to disrupt social harmony,” he said.CM Yogi Adityanath demands apology ahead of Akhilesh's Ayodhya visitAkhilesh's post came amid a political exchange over his proposed December 12 visit to Ayodhya, where he is scheduled to visit the Ram Temple and Hanumangarhi along with his wife, Dimple Yadav. The visit, announced by former SP MLA Pawan Pandey, would be Akhilesh's first to the Ram Temple since its inauguration in January 2024.Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Saturday took an apparent swipe at the SP chief, saying those who had ordered firing on Ram devotees and subjected saints to lathicharge should apologise before visiting the temple.“Those who had neglected and insulted (Ayodhya), who had opened fire on Ram devotees and subjected saints to lathicharge, should certainly come to Ayodhya, but only after apologising. Let them apologise once to Ram devotees and once to the saints. Let them repent for their actions,” Adityanath said at the 10th edition of Deepotsav in Ayodhya, according to PTI.Although he did not name any person or the party, the remarks came hours after the announcement of the proposed temple visit.Read more: 'First apologise to devotees, saints' - UP CM Yogi ahead of Akhilesh Yadav's Ram Temple visitRecalling the Ram Janmabhoomi movement, Adityanath criticised previous governments over the firing on kar sevaks and the alleged neglect of Ayodhya.“There was a time when even uttering the name of Shri Ram in Ayodhya invited lathis and bullets. Banning the very name of Ram in this city was a sin. Ayodhya was neglected and almost consigned to oblivion. Today, that very Ayodhya has come alive again, reminding us of the Treta Yuga,” he said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia downs missiles fired at Riyadh after Houthi attack on pipeline
articles.summary: Saudi forces intercept two missiles fired towards Riyadh, hours after reporting damage to key East-West pipeline.
articles.body:
The Saudi Arabia-led coalition fighting Yemen’s Houthis has announced it intercepted two missiles fired towards the kingdom’s capital, Riyadh, and another aimed at its southern region.

Major-General Turki al-Maliki, a spokesperson for the coalition, blamed the Iran-backed Houthis for Tuesday’s attacks.

In a series of posts on X, he said a ballistic missile and a cruise missile were intercepted and destroyed over Riyadh, while a second ballistic missile was downed over the southern part of the country.

Multiple explosions were heard in Riyadh, according to the AFP news agency, and residents received text-message alerts instructing them to take shelter due to an “aerial threat”.

A subsequent message from the country’s civil defence agency said the danger had passed.

There was no immediate comment from the Houthis.

The strikes were the latest in a series of attacks on Saudi Arabia as fighting rages in Yemen between the Houthis and the country’s internationally recognised government, backed by Riyadh.

The coalition has supported a Yemeni government offensive to retake territory with air strikes, while the Houthis have repeatedly struck Saudi oil infrastructure, including refineries and storage facilities, with drones and missiles.

On Monday, the East-West oil pipeline in the Medina region was attacked again . A Saudi Energy Ministry official told the state-run SPA news agency the strike caused a “limited fire” that was extinguished. The official said that “pipeline operations were unaffected”.

The pipeline is a vital route for Saudi oil exports due to Tehran’s restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz following the US-Israel war against Iran. The pipeline has come under attack several times as the war on Iran fuels a global energy crisis .

On Sunday, the Houthis also said they attacked Riyadh’s business district.

Saudi officials said falling debris from an “attempted attack” had caused minor damage to the Aramco Tower.

Images released by the SPA showed the deputy governor of the Riyadh region and other officials inspecting the building, with damage visible on several floors.

articles.title: Taiwan monitors China's 'area denial' exercises as naval activity intensifies
articles.summary: China has conducted military exercises aimed at restricting access to parts of the western pacific, deploying its Liaoning aircraft carrier group
articles.body: China has conducted military exercises aimed at restricting access to parts of the western pacific, deploying its Liaoning aircraft carrier group alongside other naval formations, Taiwan's Defence Minister Wellington Koo said on Tuesday, amid reports of increased Chinese military activity in the region.Beijing considers democratically governed Taiwan part of its territory and regularly deploys military aircraft and naval vessels near the island, activities that Taipei views as a growing security threat, according to news agency Reuters.Last week, Taiwan's national security council secretary-general Joseph Wu shared details on X of deployments involving more than 100 Chinese navy and coast guard vessels operating near Taiwan, across the South China Sea and into the pacific ocean.Taiwan's defence ministry also reported a significant increase in Chinese military aircraft operating around the island last week, although Beijing has not officially announced any military exercises."China has indeed conducted area denial drills in the western pacific with the Liaoning carrier group and other naval training formations," Koo told reporters at parliament.What are area-denial military drills?Anti-access/area denial (A2AD) operations are military strategies designed to prevent external forces from entering or intervening in a particular conflict zone. In the case of Taiwan, such capabilities could be used to obstruct the United States and its allies from providing military assistance to the island in the event of a Chinese attack.China's Defence Ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment.Last month, however, the ministry described the Liaoning carrier group's operations in the Western Pacific as part of its annual training programme. It said the exercises were intended to assess the carrier's long-range operational and open-ocean combat capabilities and were not directed against any specific country.Taiwan monitors China's military movementsThe latest Chinese military activities come ahead of next week's asia-pacific economic cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, where US President Donald Trump is expected to meet Chinese president Xi Jinping. Taiwan is also preparing for local elections scheduled towards the end of this month.Koo said Taiwan's armed forces were closely tracking China's military movements and developments in the region.He warned that such military pressure could threaten peace and stability across the Indo-Pacific.Taiwan would continue using joint intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance operations, while sharing information with allied countries to monitor China's activities and take appropriate measures, he added.Beijing has repeatedly refused to rule out the use of force to bring Taiwan under its control, although it maintains that peaceful reunification remains its preferred approach.Taipei, meanwhile, rejects China's sovereignty claims, maintaining that Taiwan's future can only be determined by its people.You use AI every day. articles.title: Google cybersecurity company Wiz flew employees to Thailand, company with roots in Israel made Katy Perry perform at the offsite event; her appearance has sparked protests as ...
articles.summary: Wiz flew employees to Thailand for a five-day retreat.
articles.body: ​Wiz flew employees to Thailand for a five-day retreat. The Google-owned cybersecurity company, founded by Israeli entrepreneurs, reportedly arranged a surprise private performance by Katy Perry during the holiday in Khao Lak. According to a Calcalist report, her appearance drew online criticism, with users questioning her decision to perform for the company and challenging celebrities who pair public social stances with lucrative private bookings.​The trip included luxury resort accommodation and parties, estimated at tens of millions of shekels. Perry’s performance alone reportedly cost between $3 million and $4 million, including her fee and production costs. The concert, which featured several of her hits, including “I Kissed a Girl,” capped off the employee getaway.​Why Katy Perry’s Wiz concert drew criticism onlineUsers on the international music forum ATRL opened a discussion about the performance and criticised Perry’s participation, Ynet reported.​One commenter referred to posts by Thai citizens complaining about what they described as Zionist tourists, adding that those visitors were now bringing Perry with them. Another expressed renewed disappointment in the singer. A third questioned artists who publicly take social positions while accepting substantial payments to entertain wealthy individuals and major companies.​The reported reaction centres on online criticism. The estimated $3 million to $4 million concert cost includes production expenses, meaning the figure does not represent Perry’s personal fee alone.​Katty Perry’s private performance in Australia faced a pro-Palestinian protest​Perry also performed at Australian billionaire Anthony Pratt’s Melbourne estate in February 2024, at an event attended by Australia’s prime minister and other senior figures.​According to Australian outlet Nine, she was paid about A$1.5 million for the appearance. A Nine entertainment report separately estimated that a private booking could cost between A$2 million and A$3 million.​Dozens of pro-Palestinian demonstrators gathered outside the estate. They protested against those attending and drew attention to the bombing and hunger faced by people in Gaza.​Wiz’s history of costly employee retreats and celebrity performances​Google agreed in March 2025 to acquire Wiz for $32 billion. The deal closed in March 2026, merging the cybersecurity business into Google Cloud.​Wiz, founded by Assaf Rappaport and his partners, has a history of expensive employee celebrations. Its ABBA-inspired “Wizcotheque” Purim party at Expo Tel Aviv reportedly cost about 10 million shekels and featured more than 20 Israeli artists, including Ninet Tayeb, Shiri Maimon and Sarit Hadad.​The company also previously took employees to Mauritius for activities modelled on “Survivor.” Its annual sales event in Las Vegas in March featured rapper Pitbull, with a production built around a fictional airline called “WizAir.”​You use AI every day. articles.title: Dyson launches Hot+Cool HF1 fan heater, Cool tower fan in India, price starts at Rs 27,900
articles.summary: Dyson has expanded its home comfort portfolio in India with the launch of the Dyson Hot+Cool HF1 Remote Link Pre-heat heater and cooling fan and the Dyson
articles.body: Dyson has expanded its home comfort portfolio in India with the launch of the Dyson Hot+Cool HF1 Remote Link Pre-heat heater and cooling fan and the Dyson Cool tower fan. The new bladeless devices are powered by the company's Air Multiplier technology and are designed to provide year-round thermal comfort, offering both heating and cooling capabilities depending on seasonal requirements. According to the company, the two new products build on more than three decades of Dyson's expertise in airflow engineering. Using technologies such as computational fluid dynamics, airflow mapping and acoustic engineering, the machines are designed to project air efficiently without exposed spinning blades.Dyson said both products use its proprietary Air Multiplier technology, which draws in surrounding air and amplifies it to generate a smooth and powerful airflow for cooling or heating.Dyson Hot+Cool HF1 offers heating and cooling in one machineThe Dyson Hot+Cool HF1 is a 2-in-1 fan heater that can function as both a room heater during winter and a cooling fan during summer. The company claims the device can increase the temperature of an entire room by one degree Celsius in as little as 100 seconds. The machine features an intelligent temperature control system with an integrated sensor that automatically maintains the desired room temperature, helping improve energy efficiency. It also includes a sleep mode that dims the display, reduces operational noise and maintains the selected temperature overnight.Dyson says the HF1 is 25% quieter than its predecessor thanks to improvements in airflow and compressor technology. Users can choose from up to 10 airflow settings and temperature controls reaching up to 32 degrees Celsius. The device also supports 70-degree oscillation, manual tilt adjustments and automatic shut-off if tipped over. A key highlight is connected functionality. Dyson says the HF1 is its first connected fan heater, allowing users to adjust settings directly on the machine, through the supplied remote control or via the MyDyson app.Dyson Cool tower fan focuses on personal coolingAlongside the HF1, Dyson has introduced the Dyson Cool tower fan, a bladeless cooling solution aimed at delivering high-velocity airflow for personal comfort. The fan offers ten airflow settings, remote control operation and a sleep timer that allows users to schedule automatic shut-off. Dyson says the machine has been acoustically engineered with a Helmholtz cavity in the base to reduce noise while maintaining airflow performance. The bladeless design also makes the fan easier to clean compared to conventional fans with grilles and exposed blades.Durability and testingDyson said its machines undergo extensive reliability and endurance testing before launch. The company uses a range of testing methods, including destructive and performance tests, while technologies such as Laser Doppler Anemometry are employed to analyse airflow patterns and identify potential design improvements.Price and availabilityThe Dyson Hot+Cool HF1 Remote Link Pre-heat heater and cooling fan has been priced at Rs 38,900, while the Dyson Cool tower fan costs Rs 27,900. Both products are available through Dyson's official website and Dyson Demo stores across India.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.body: KANPUR: Geeta Sachan, a woman pursuing her studies in Italy, was arrested and later released by a court after the Thar she was allegedly driving hit a 55-year-old scooter rider in Kanpur and dragged him and his vehicle for nearly 20 metres.The victim, Santosh Singh Chauhan, an LIC agent, was just 500 metres from home after stepping out to buy a saree for his wife.The accident took place on Saturday evening in the Awas Vikas 3 area of Kalyanpur, around 500 metres from the victim's home.Chauhan, a resident of Swaraj Nagar in Panki, was riding his scooter when the speeding Thar hit him.The impact dragged him and his scooter for about 20 metres before the SUV crashed into a green area outside a house.The vehicle first hit the house of Professor Kailash before crashing into the boundary wall of Anita Mahevan's house, residents said.Chauhan's son, Rahul, identified his father's body. He said Chauhan had left home telling the family that he would return shortly.Witnesses said two young women and a man travelling in the Thar screamed after the accident but later left the spot in another car.The SUV, which had 'Kisan Union' written on its front and 'Krishna Group' on its rear, was seized by police.
